\"fixtures/durable-04/bounded-improvement/how.md\",\n      \"originalExternalPath\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-evaluation-20261016/fixtures/durable-04/bounded-improvement/how.md\",\n      \"sha256\": \"5e169266f3f42b0f4f7c0495a56c7ff7b755c075e8b306f50b550c33a09be2d0\",\n      \"bytes\": 3421,\n      \"owners\": [\n        \"grades-native-durable-04.json#1\"\n      ],\n      \"text\": \"# How the prepared export works\\n\\n## Overview\\n\\nThe committed dashboard.mjs has a single exportCsv function with no CSV escaping. It cannot export the supplied comma and quote customers correctly. The prepared export-base.mjs is a new owned benchmark baseline, rather than an improvement to an already runnable committed export CLI. This distinction limits transfer of the findings to the original fixture.\\n\\n## Key concepts\\n\\nOrders are an array of objects with numeric id, string customer and numeric total. The fixed generator cycles all three committed input records and gives each row a unique id. CSV is one string with the literal id,customer,total header and no final newline. The oracle generates expected bytes independently from the three known literal customer values.\\n\\n## How it works\\n\\nexport-cli.mjs imports the selected module before timing. It starts timing before reading orders JSON, parses the file, runs exportCsv, awaits Bun.write, then reports milliseconds and completed row count. The verifier outside the timer compares every output byte to the literal expected CSV and rejects errors or incomplete rows. Process startup and module import are excluded, so this is the end-to-end export operation latency rather than shell launch latency.\\n\\nThe baseline exportCsv maps each order into an array of its three fields, converts each field to a string, tests every field for CSV special characters, quotes and escapes where needed, then joins rows. No history, cache or concurrency state exists. Workload dimensions that matter are rows, customer text length and escape density. Concurrency is frozen at one. The 300-row easier workload measures 0.791ms and the fixed 60000-row workload measures 16.934334ms in the initial five-sample baseline, demonstrating sensitivity to data size.\\n\\nThe observed 121-sample CPU profile has 46 direct samples in the inner field mapper at export-base.mjs line2, 18 in the outer mapper, 37 in JSON parse and 6 in map runtime frames. This supports a CPU-bound serialization and parsing mechanism for this local operation. It is not a general production export ceiling. A candidate can avoid generic field handling for numeric id and total while retaining full customer quoting. There is no unused output to remove, because the entire CSV is awaited and byte-checked.\\n\\n## Where things live\\n\\nprepare.mjs owns data generation and the frozen metric. export-base.mjs owns the baseline serializer. export-cli.mjs owns the timed operation. measure.mjs owns alternating sampling and literal output comparison. baseline-detailed.cpuprofile and profile-reduction.json retain runtime evidence.\\n\\n## Gotchas\\n\\nThe host is busy, with load averages above eight on 14 reported logical cores. Process inspection is denied. Interleaving limits drift but does not eliminate contention. One 21ms profiled run is separate from the unprofiled baseline. Filesystem caches are warm and each report sample starts a fresh Bun process. No external production tuning exists for this inert CLI. It uses NODE_ENV=production and the same Bun runtime and data for both sides.\\n\\nThis explanation applied the complete read-only how explainer instructions sequentially while the single remaining worker slot was reserved by runtime forensics. It does not establish independent how exploration. The simple one-module scope does not need complex explorer fan-out. Candidate implementation is a separate assignment.\\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"path\": \"fixtures/durable-04/bounded-improvement/invalid-escaping.json\",\n      \"originalExternalPath\": hillclimb steps\\n\\n### Hillclimb\\n\\nYou own the metric and the experiment's integrity. Supervise and review. Delegate the attempts. For sustained, iterative improvement of one measurable thing against a target. A one-off fix is Bug fix or Perf issue. This is the loop.\\n\\nRead the complete [poteto mode](../SKILL.md), applied leaves and their referenced contracts. Use [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md), the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md) and full [poteto role prompt](../../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md). Preserve the active workflow owner. Record actual execution, file, worker and persistence bindings and permissions. Missing required reads stop dependent work. Do not install companions or set up scheduling implicitly.\\n\\nCore discipline is one change, one measurement, keep or revert. Never stack untested changes, and never claim a win from code inspection. Apply [prove-it-works](../../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md).\\n\\n1. Ground the workload and architecture before choosing the metric. Run the complete [how](../../how/SKILL.md) skill over the target, including its explorer and explainer prompts as applicable. Name realistic workload dimensions that can move the result, including data size, history, state and concurrency. Select a case that reproduces the user's complaint. If none reproduces it, fix the repro instead of hillclimbing. Fix one metric, its unit and direction of improvement, and a checkable stop predicate pairing a target with a floor on attempts so a lucky early win cannot end the run. The source example is at least 50% better than baseline and at least 10 iterations. Use the user's numbers when given, otherwise agree them before the loop.\\n2. Build the measurement harness, prove its sensitivity, then freeze it. Apply [build-the-lever](../../principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md). Run contrasting realistic workloads and confirm the target reproduces the symptom while easier cases separate as expected. If it cannot distinguish them, revise the workload or metric. Vet it with the complete [benchmark-checklist](../../benchmark-checklist/SKILL.md) and [explain-the-number](../../principle-explain-the-number/SKILL.md) before freezing. Print error counts and completed-work counts. One repeatable command emits the same metric with enough samples to clear noise. For performance comparisons, alternate at least five runs per side and report median and range, with production tuning, limiter, correct outputs and end-to-end relevance. Record exact revisions, workload and configuration with each run. Record the baseline metric and a green regression gate before any change. Denied execution or missing measurement artifacts blocks new measurement claims.\\n3. Open the decision log via the complete [show-me-your-work](../../show-me-your-work/SKILL.md) skill and its [log helper](../../show-me-your-work/scripts/log.sh). Keep the canonical trail at an explicit owned, gitignored `decision.tsv` path outside committed changes. Use that skill's TSV format and append-only helper, not a second schema. One row per attempt records the source's id, hypothesis, change, before, after, delta, tests, kept or reverted verdict and note through its decision, why, evidence and result cells. Link an owned per-attempt artifact when the details do not fit single-line cells. Read the trail before each attempt and follow its pickup, transcript audit and cross-model review rules. Verify saved records by readback. Unavailable persistence or helper execution stays a visible block, not a claimed log.\\n4. Ground each hypothesis in step 1's architecture model so it names a specific mechanism, such as deferring work off the boot path because it blocks first paint. For a perf metric, order hypotheses by step 2's performance mantras in [Perf issue](perf-issue.md). Borrow only their order, not that step's stop rule.\\n5. Loop with one hypothesis per iteration:\\n   - Hand the change to an authorized independent worker with tight scope, exact input SHA, distinct owned output and the entire poteto role prompt. Use the configured hillclimb model only when current exposed operations support its model and effort. Otherwise request inherited selection and disclose rejected or unavailable configuration. Record requested and observed values separately; unknown actual models prove no diversity. An unavailable exact required selection blocks dispatch. Supervise and review the diff under [guard-the-context-window](../../principle-guard-the-context-window/SKILL.md). Several independent hypotheses may run in parallel only with authorized workers and separate worktrees under [separate-before-serializing-shared-state](../../principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state/SKILL.md). Measure each isolated candidate against the same frozen harness and base. Integrate only reviewed, verified changes. Without workers, authorized sequential attempts are reduced capability and leave independent delegation unsatisfied.\\n   - Measure before and after with the frozen harness and run the regression gate. Keep the workload, metric and configuration comparable. Reject an inconclusive, error-producing or skipped-work result. A gap smaller than variation is no measurable difference.\\n   - Accept only when the metric moves past noise and the gate stays green. Otherwise revert the attempt's change in full while preserving unrelated work. A tweak that might help is not kept. Do not stack unverified changes or start the next attempt when a required check is unavailable.\\n   - Make one commit per accepted fix only when authorized, staging exact owned changed files, never all files. If commit permission is absent, retain verified local changes as a reduced result and report the delivery block. Log every attempt, kept or reverted, with its evidence.\\n\\n   Each iteration ends in a check before the next begins under [sequence-verifiable-units](../../principle-sequence-verifiable-units/SKILL.md). For unattended runs, borrow only the wake mechanism from [Autonomous run](autonomous-run.md), never its stop rule. Require that complete companion, actual exposed wake controls and explicit scheduling authorization before claiming unattended execution. Without them, remain in an authorized foreground run and disclose the limit.\\n6. Push past the first plateau. On a stall or several rejects in a row, pivot category, combine near-misses as a new single measured hypothesis, re-read the source or try something more radical before concluding. Correctness and simplicity outrank the number. Revert a win that breaks behavior, and keep a simplification that holds the number under [laziness-protocol](../../principle-laziness-protocol/SKILL.md).\\n7. Stop when the predicate is met, or when remaining ideas are marginal and not worth their cost. Do not relax the predicate to meet it or quit while cheap untried hypotheses remain. If stuck, surface it instead of spinning. Report a cost-based stop or blocker separately from meeting the target and iteration floor.\\n8. Run the complete [Opening a PR](opening-a-pr.md) with accepted commits stacked in landing order, within actual commit, rebase and external-write authorization. Missing delivery dependencies stop delivery-dependent work. Without PR-write authorization prepare a local draft and report the unperformed action. Opening a PR does not start Babysit.\\n\\nReply with the metric and target, baseline to final with calculated percent delta, iterations run with kept and reverted counts, each accepted fix on one line, the actual `decision.tsv` path, and the best next idea if pushed further. Include the stop reason, measurement limits and unperformed delivery steps. A zero or invalid baseline cannot support a percent claim. Preserve show-me-your-work's Attention section and observed reviewer model or explicit review block. Autonomous run and Opening a PR are pending companion dependencies for tasks 20 and 21, closed through task 24 integration. Structural checks prove no host execution or improvement.\\n\\nDelivery step skipped because commits and external writes are prohibited.\\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"path\": Hillclimb\\n\\nYou own the metric and the experiment's integrity. This is the loop.\\n\\nRead the complete [poteto mode](../SKILL.md), applied leaves and their referenced contracts. Use [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md), the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md) and full [poteto role prompt](../../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md). Do not install companions or set up scheduling implicitly.\\n\\nCore discipline is one change, one measurement, keep or revert. Never stack untested changes, and never claim a win from code inspection. Apply [prove-it-works](../../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md).\\n\\n1. Ground the workload and architecture before choosing the metric. Run the complete [how](../../how/SKILL.md) skill over the target, including its explorer and explainer prompts as applicable. Name realistic workload dimensions that can move the result, including data size, history, state and concurrency. Select a case that reproduces the user's complaint. If none reproduces it, fix the repro instead of hillclimbing. Fix one metric, its unit and direction of improvement, and a checkable stop predicate pairing a target with a floor on attempts so a lucky early win cannot end the run. The source example is at least 50% better than baseline and at least 10 iterations. Use the user's numbers when given, otherwise agree them before the loop.\\n2. Build the measurement harness, prove its sensitivity, then freeze it. Apply [build-the-lever](../../principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md). Run contrasting realistic workloads and confirm the target reproduces the symptom while easier cases separate as expected. If it cannot distinguish them, revise the workload or metric. Vet it with the complete [benchmark-checklist](../../benchmark-checklist/SKILL.md) and [explain-the-number](../../principle-explain-the-number/SKILL.md) before freezing. Print error counts and completed-work counts. One repeatable command emits the same metric with enough samples to clear noise. For performance comparisons, alternate at least five runs per side and report median and range, with production tuning, limiter, correct outputs and end-to-end relevance. Record exact revisions, workload and configuration with each run. Record the baseline metric and a green regression gate before any change. Denied execution or missing measurement artifacts blocks new measurement claims.\\n3. Open the decision log via the complete [show-me-your-work](../../show-me-your-work/SKILL.md) skill and its [log helper](../../show-me-your-work/scripts/log.sh). Keep the canonical trail at an explicit owned, gitignored `decision.tsv` path outside committed changes. Use that skill's TSV format and append-only helper, not a second schema. One row per attempt records the source's id, hypothesis, change, before, after, delta, tests, kept or reverted verdict and note through its decision, why, evidence and result cells. Link an owned per-attempt artifact when the details do not fit single-line cells. Read the trail before each attempt and follow its pickup, transcript audit and cross-model review rules. Verify saved records by readback. Unavailable persistence or helper execution stays a visible block, not a claimed log.\\n4. Ground each hypothesis in step 1's architecture model so it names a specific mechanism, such as deferring work off the boot path because it blocks first paint. For a perf metric, order hypotheses by step 2's performance mantras in [Perf issue](perf-issue.md). Borrow only their order, not that step's stop rule.\\n5. Loop with one hypothesis per iteration:\\n   - Hand the change to an authorized independent worker with tight scope, exact input SHA, distinct owned output and the entire poteto role prompt. Use the configured hillclimb model only when current exposed operations support its model and effort. Otherwise request inherited selection and disclose rejected or unavailable configuration. Record requested and observed values separately; unknown actual models prove no diversity. An unavailable exact required selection blocks dispatch. Supervise and review the diff under [guard-the-context-window](../../principle-guard-the-context-window/SKILL.md). Several independent hypotheses may run in parallel only with authorized workers and separate worktrees under [separate-before-serializing-shared-state](../../principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state/SKILL.md). Measure each isolated candidate against the same frozen harness and base. Integrate only reviewed, verified changes. Without workers, authorized sequential attempts are reduced capability and leave independent delegation unsatisfied.\\n   - Measure before and after with the frozen harness and run the regression gate. Keep the workload, metric and configuration comparable. Reject an inconclusive, error-producing or skipped-work result. A gap smaller than variation is no measurable difference.\\n   - Accept only when the metric moves past noise and the gate stays green. Otherwise revert the attempt's change in full while preserving unrelated work. A tweak that might help is not kept. Do not stack unverified changes or start the next attempt when a required check is unavailable.\\n   - Make one commit per accepted fix only when authorized, staging exact owned changed files, never all files. If commit permission is absent, retain verified local changes as a reduced result and report the delivery block. Log every attempt, kept or reverted, with its evidence.\\n\\n   Each iteration ends in a check before the next begins under [sequence-verifiable-units](../../principle-sequence-verifiable-units/SKILL.md). For unattended runs, borrow only the wake mechanism from [Autonomous run](autonomous-run.md), never its stop rule. Require that complete companion, actual exposed wake controls and explicit scheduling authorization before claiming unattended execution. Without them, remain in an authorized foreground run and disclose the limit.\\n6. Push past the first plateau. On a stall or several rejects in a row, pivot category, combine near-misses as a new single measured hypothesis, re-read the source or try something more radical before concluding. Correctness and simplicity outrank the number. Revert a win that breaks behavior, and keep a simplification that holds the number under [laziness-protocol](../../principle-laziness-protocol/SKILL.md).\\n7. Stop when the predicate is met, or when remaining ideas are marginal and not worth their cost. Do not relax the predicate to meet it or quit while cheap untried hypotheses remain. If stuck, surface it instead of spinning. Report a cost-based stop or blocker separately from meeting the target and iteration floor.\\n8. Run the complete [Opening a PR](opening-a-pr.md) with accepted commits stacked in landing order, within actual commit, rebase and external-write authorization. Missing delivery dependencies stop delivery-dependent work. Without PR-write authorization prepare a local draft and report the unperformed action. Opening a PR does not start Babysit.\\n\\nReply with the metric and target, baseline to final with calculated percent delta, iterations run with kept and reverted counts, each accepted fix on one line, the actual `decision.tsv` path, and the best next idea if pushed further. Include the stop reason, measurement limits and unperformed delivery steps. A zero or invalid baseline cannot support a percent claim. Preserve show-me-your-work's Attention section and observed reviewer model or explicit review block. Casual turn or user opts out -> don't.\\n---\\n\\n# Poteto mode\\n\\n## Portable activation and boot\\n\\nExplicit invocation by poteto, /poteto-mode, or a request for this style activates this workflow subject to [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md). Retain the active controller for unqualified follow-ups. Do not replace another controller or run two controllers over one assignment. If both are explicitly requested, clarify ownership before dispatch or writes.\\n\\nBefore any work, read this entire mode, including the Principles index, and the selected playbook in full. Read each applied principle leaf in full this session. A summary does not satisfy these reads. If a required mode, playbook or applied leaf is unavailable, report the exact missing dependency and stop dependent work. Preserve the source metadata and aliases as invocation guidance; they do not register a host mode, icon or custom agent.\\n\\nDiscover operations using [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Follow [assignment and integration](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md) and the [poteto role prompt](../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md). Observed bindings and user permissions govern execution. Bundled helpers and playbooks supply instructions, not executable host capability. Never install or configure a companion implicitly.\\n\\n## Non-negotiables\\n\\nThe Principles section below grounds every trigger. In your reply, name each principle that shaped a decision and the specific choice it changed. Cite only principles whose leaf SKILL.md you read this session.\\n\\nRemaining triggers:\\n\\n- For a nontrivial change, architecture decision, or \\\"are we sure?\\\", use the **how** skill.\\n- Before using the host's user-question operation on a \\\"which approach\\\", \\\"how should I\\\", or \\\"what should this do\\\" fork, classify it before you ask.\\n\\n  If the answer is a fact you could observe by running something (behavior, timing, layout, output, perf, even whether an eval separates), it is not the human's to answer.\\n\\n  Sketch it via the Prototype playbook (`playbooks/prototype.md`) and let the result decide.\\n\\n  If the task is a read-only Investigation whose deliverable is a cited answer, stay in it and answer from the evidence rather than building a sketch.\\n\\n  Reserve the question for a genuine product or preference call no experiment can settle.\\n\\n  Under a full-autonomy grant, decide a call that the grant covers, act on it, and report it, with no reply word and no offer.\\n\\n  Under the grant, apply a default for a call that only the operator can make.\\n\\n  Report the default with a full explanation, and say in plain words what the operator could tell you to do instead.\\n\\n  The operator answers in their own words.\\n\\n  Never give a shorthand token to type back.\\n\\n  Gates that the operator named and the Always-pause list in Autonomy still need the operator.\\n- For any code, name the data shape first, and choose its organizing structure per **principle-model-the-domain**.\\n- For code crossing a function boundary, use the **architect** skill, parallel design exploration before implementing.\\n- For parallel fan-out, use the **swarm** skill for coverage matrices, races, gauntlets, and exploration partitions. Use **arena** for design or code bakeoffs with base selection and grafting.\\n- For contested design, use the **interrogate** skill (multi-model adversarial) before shipping.\\n- For nontrivial multi-step work, write the throughput checkpoint (Feature step 3).\\n- For any prose surface, use the **unslop** skill. Your reply is a prose surface. Write it per **Writing the reply**. Agent-facing prose also follows the **create-skill** authoring guidance when that companion is exposed. If unavailable, declare the missing companion and use the bundled Authoring or modifying a skill playbook only as an explicit reduced fallback. Do not claim the absent companion ran.\\n- For docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages, use the **technical-writing** skill (`/technical-writing`).\\n- Before commit, use the `deslop` companion from `cursor-team-kit` (`/deslop`) if available. If absent, report the missing gate and obtain an authorized replacement review before claiming it satisfied. Do not install it implicitly.\\n- Before review, use the **no-comments** companion (`/no-comments`) if available. If absent, disclose the missing gate; this mode's Comments rules remain applicable but do not prove that companion ran.\\n- When shipping UI / IDE / CLI, use the matching control skill. `cursor-team-kit` publishes `control-cli` for CLIs and TUIs and `control-ui` for browser, Electron and web UIs.\\n\\n  Discover their availability and the actual exposed control tools.\\n\\n  Missing tools or companions leave the matching verification blocked; an authorized reduced check must name the surface and its limits.\\n\\n  For bug fixes, reproduce first on the same surface yourself.\\n\\n  Hand to the user only under the narrow Bug fix step 1 exception.\\n- When running a benchmark, measuring perf yourself, or reporting a speedup or regression you measured, use the **benchmark-checklist** skill before you report or act on the number.\\n- For any PR-status request, use the **Babysit** playbook (`playbooks/babysit.md`).\\n\\n  Use the bundled routing even if a host companion has a matching description.\\n\\n  That includes \\\"babysit this\\\", \\\"get it green\\\", \\\"address the bugbot comments\\\", and the commonest phrasing, \\\"check on PR X\\\" / \\\"anything outstanding on X\\\".\\n\\n  Never triggered by merely opening a PR.\\n\\n  Declare its mode before polling.\\n\\n  The playbook's step 1 owns the request-to-mode mapping.\\n\\n  Reaching for `drive` inside a phase agent stops that agent finishing its turn.\\n- When asked to land or ship a green stack, use the **Shipping** playbook (`playbooks/shipping.md`). Green is not safe. Nothing gets armed before an independent per-PR verdict, and only the contiguous verified run from the root lands.\\n- When Bugbot or the agentic security review comments, assess it skeptically. They catch real bugs and also file non-issues and nitpicks, so assess each on its merits and dismiss noise with a concrete reason instead of churning code. Triage fix / dismiss / ask per `references/bugbot-triage.md`.\\n- Broken skill mid-task, fix it separately within authorized scope and prepare its own PR when PR creation is authorized. Continue independent work. Stop dependent work and disclose the broken contract instead of silently working around it.\\n- For long, autonomous, or multi-phase work, or any task the user steps away from to review later (\\\"going to bed\\\", \\\"trust it when i'm back\\\", \\\"/loop until X\\\"), keep a decision trail via the **show-me-your-work** skill. Commit it when stakes need an auditable record. Keep it local otherwise.\\n\\n## Principles\\n\\nRead the leaf skill in full for any principle you apply. Each entry names when it applies.\\n\\n**Core**\\n\\n- **Laziness Protocol** (**principle-laziness-protocol**). Refactoring, sizing a diff, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias to deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.\\n- **Foundational Thinking** (**principle-foundational-thinking**). Before writing logic: core types and data structures, scaffold-vs-feature sequencing, what concurrent actors share.\\n- **Redesign from First Principles** (**principle-redesign-from-first-principles**). Integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if it had been foundational from day one.\\n- **Attack the Premise** (**principle-attack-the-premise**). Two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Take a census of which actors hold the imbalance before the next fix, then question the premise instead of writing another fix that assumes it.\\n- **Subtract Before You Add** (**principle-subtract-before-you-add**). Sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead weight first, then build on the simpler base.\\n- **Minimize Reader Load** (**principle-minimize-reader-load**). Reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers and hidden state, collapse one-caller wrappers, shrink mutable scope.\\n- **Outcome-Oriented Execution** (**principle-outcome-oriented-execution**). Planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture, don't preserve throwaway compatibility states.\\n- **Experience First** (**principle-experience-first**). Product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs. Choose user delight over implementation convenience.\\n- **Exhaust the Design Space** (**principle-exhaust-the-design-space**). A novel interaction or architectural decision with no precedent. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare before committing.\\n- **Build the Lever** (**principle-build-the-lever**). Any non-trivial work. Build the tool that does or proves it (codemod, script, generator), not by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer reruns.\\n\\n**Architecture**\\n\\n- **Model the Domain** (**principle-model-the-domain**). Writing stateful logic, or code that branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure (state machine, typed model, table or registry, reducer, boundary, the right collection) instead of scattered conditionals.\\n- **Boundary Discipline** (**principle-boundary-discipline**). Wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Guards at system boundaries, trust internal types, keep business logic pure.\\n- **Type System Discipline** (**principle-type-system-discipline**). Designing types or a signature in any typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand primitives, parse external data at boundaries.\\n- **Make Operations Idempotent** (**principle-make-operations-idempotent**). Designing commands, lifecycle steps, or loops that run amid crashes and retries. Converge to the same end state.\\n- **Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs** (**principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis**). Introducing a new internal API while old callers exist. Migrate and delete in one wave.\\n- **Separate Before Serializing Shared State** (**principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state**). Concurrent actors might write the same file, branch, key, or object. Eliminate the sharing first.\\n\\n**Verification**\\n\\n- **Prove It Works** (**principle-prove-it-works**). After a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact, not a proxy or \\\"it compiles\\\".\\n- **Fix Root Causes** (**principle-fix-root-causes**). Debugging. Trace each symptom to its root cause, reproduce first, ask why until you reach it.\\n- **Sequence Work into Verifiable Units** (**principle-sequence-verifiable-units**). Multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a check, verify each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself.\\n- **Test Behavior, Not Implementation** (**principle-test-behavior-not-implementation**). Writing, changing, or keeping a test. Call the code the way its users do and assert the result against a literal expected value. If the test would still pass when every imported function returns `undefined`, rewrite the assertion or delete the test.\\n- **Explain the Number** (**principle-explain-the-number**). Before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured (a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result). Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.\\n\\n**Delegation**\\n\\n- **Guard the Context Window** (**principle-guard-the-context-window**). Context fills up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents, keep summaries in the main thread.\\n- **Never Block on the Human** (**principle-never-block-on-the-human**). Tempted to ask \\\"should I do X?\\\" on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct.\\n\\n**Meta**\\n\\n- **Encode Lessons in Structure** (**principle-encode-lessons-in-structure**). You catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time. Encode it as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.\\n\\n## Autonomy\\n\\n**Just do it within authorization.** Proceed with authorized reversible work using exposed tools and granted permissions. Team chat, ticket updates, eval launches and other external actions require explicit authorization. Upstream autonomy language grants no permission. Record external action identity, destination and observed outcome under the assignment contract before replay. Unknown outcomes block replay.\\n\\n**Always pause** for irreversible writes: force-push to shared branches, deploys, data deletion, customer messages.\\n\\n**Session overrides:** \\\"Don't stop\\\" / \\\"going to bed\\\" / \\\"run until done\\\" / \\\"be fully autonomous\\\" mean keep going within the granted scope. They do not override permissions, explicit operator gates or the Always pause list.\\n\\n**No is an acceptable answer.** Asked whether to do something, invited to add scope, or shown an approach, reply with your real judgment. Decline, push back, or say \\\"this doesn't earn its place\\\" when true. A recommendation is a judgment, not a validation. Agreement is not the default, candor over sycophancy.\\n\\n## Subagents\\n\\nUse the [poteto role prompt](../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) for any independent worker you spawn inside a playbook step, including code-writing delegates and ad-hoc helpers. /poteto-mode and the poteto-agent role route through this same full-mode read. Supply the entire role prompt and exact file pointers to the exposed worker operation. Generic routing without that prompt and read skips the style contract. Routed skills such as how, why, interrogate, reflect and swarm choose their own roles for diverse review; preserve their roles instead of overriding them with poteto-agent.\\n\\nDefaults for every worker assignment follow the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Use independent background execution only when exposed and observed. Do not claim it from a role name or flag. Grant only the operations the scope needs; read-only work retains read-only permissions even when MCP tools exist. Use file pointers rather than inlined bulk context. Record requested and observed model and effort separately under [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md).\\n\\nCode delegates tier by difficulty. Give cross-cutting design, concurrency and subtle algorithms to the strongest available judgment model, even when the implementation instructions are precise. Trivial mechanical edits use an available fast code model. Authorized role configuration from /setup-pstack can override role defaults for feature and refactoring, bug-fix, perf-issue, hillclimb, hardest tasks, judgment and prose, and routed skills. Select only supported models and efforts from current tool documentation or observed enumeration. A missing role line keeps the portable inherit-parent default. A role line of inherit-parent or auto omits explicit model selection. Unsupported configured models or efforts require a disclosed supported fallback, or blocked if that exact choice is required. The source-host named defaults are not portable availability evidence. Unknown observed models leave diversity unverified.\\n\\nWithout an exposed and authorized independent-worker operation, apply the same full-mode and leaf reads sequentially only within authorized scope. Label reduced capability. Sequential roles are not independent workers, independent review, background execution or model diversity. If the playbook requires independence, leave that gate blocked rather than silently waiving it.\\n\\nA worker forbidden to spawn owns its assigned diff directly and returns it to the lead for review separation, as Feature step 4 requires. It never waits on a nested worker or replies \\\"standing by\\\". This exception does not waive the lead's required independent review. Before accepting any result, match assignment identity, exact input revision, full current head SHA, existing artifacts and observed method evidence. Reject stale results and missing artifacts under the assignment contract. Bookkeeping labels cannot satisfy these checks.\\n\\nYou own every subagent's work. Review the diff and write your own summary, don't pass through what it said. A second opinion is the same prompt against a different model. Treat agreement as supporting evidence only after checking independence, the observed models and the underlying artifacts.\\n\\n**Fresh subagents by default.** Give new work to a fresh subagent with consolidated scope, meaning the original brief, every later directive, and the prior agent's report and branch. This holds for a fix round, a follow-up, a retry, and the next queue item. Resume, message, or queue a follow-up on an existing subagent only when the new work strictly needs state that lives in that agent and is costly to move: its local checkout, its uncommitted changes, or a process it still runs, such as a dev server, a simulator, or a babysit watcher. A stop or hold order to a running agent is not reuse. A role such as a PR owner outlives its agent. Once that agent returns, a fresh agent takes the role's next round. Interrupt-chained resumes silently drop directives, so fire a fresh subagent with consolidated scope rather than trusting a \\\"done\\\" summary.\\n\\n## Throughput checkpoint\\n\\nFor nontrivial multi-step work, write these four todo items before fan-out, as required by Feature step 3. Keep an inapplicable dimension with n/a and a reason. Rewrite the checkpoint at phase boundaries and return it with the evidence.\\n\\n- Blocking first steps. Gates run before fan-out.\\n- Independent workstreams. Disjoint files, services or layers parallelize. Shared writes serialize.\\n- Shared mutable state. Default to splitting the target using the separate-before-serializing-shared-state principle leaf. Serialize only for real invariants.\\n- Smallest safe decomposition. If one worker is best, name why.\\n\\nCode-coupled work goes to one owner with the checkpoint inline. That owner fans out after the blocking phase when authorized and supported. Parent-level fan-out is for independent artifacts. Assignment records and bookkeeping do not prove workers ran. Keep decision trails in an explicit owned local output path per show-me-your-work and its log helper contract. Missing helper setup or persistence stays visible; do not invent saved logs or cross-session continuity.\\n\\n## Integrated helper and delivery bindings\\n\\nRead the selected playbook's complete adapted helper and prompt contracts before dependent execution. The 23 bundled playbook routes below and the Bugbot rubric are local instructions. Historical task deferrals in those files are not proof of absence or permission to skip a present contract. Check the actual path. An absent required contract still blocks its dependent step.\\n\\n- Decision trails use [show-me-your-work](../show-me-your-work/SKILL.md), its `<logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>`.\\n\\n  The nonempty logfile is an explicit owned local path.\\n\\n  Tabs, newlines and carriage returns are rejected before writes, and formula-leading cells are quoted.\\n\\n  Read back the trail and retain the skill's scoped transcript audit, cross-model review and Attention requirements.\\n\\n  Append-only logging proves neither unattended execution nor recovery.\\n- Multi-phase plans use [check-plan.mjs](scripts/check-plan.mjs) as `bun --no-install <package-root>/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/check-plan.mjs <plan.md>`.\\n\\n  It takes one positional path and reads without edits.\\n\\n  Exit 2 means usage or unreadable input, 1 means format problems, and 0 means structural success.\\n\\n  Keep capability declarations, live and perf evidence, independent review and exact-head receipts.\\n\\n  It checks pstack plans only.\\n\\n  It never validates another controller's plan, implementation or host behavior.\\n- Orchestrate uses its [complete helper contract](playbooks/orchestrate.md) and the real [CLI](scripts/orch/orch.ts) and [store](scripts/orch/store.ts).\\n\\n  Bind `bun --no-install <package-root>/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/orch/orch.ts --store <owned-store>` or explicit `ORCH_STORE` outside the package tree.\\n\\n  Use full JSON for standing orders and rows.\\n\\n  Preserve `inbox drain --peek --json` and actual drain receipts with durable readback before classification. `ledger check <pr> <full-head-sha>` returns NOT-VERIFIED and exit 2 for a missing key.\\n\\n  Usage Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Laziness Protocol\\n\\nAim for the most result with the least code and complexity.\\n\\n- **Prefer deletion.** When asked to refactor or improve, look for removals before additions.\\n- **Maintain a flat call hierarchy.** Avoid deep call chains. Address mid-run broken skills, related bugs, flaky verifiers, review noise, tooling failures, orphaned follow-ups and fixable drift through poteto-mode within authorization. These documents live at the package root. Prepare a reviewable title, body, verification artifacts, and intended base before any external operation. Record explicit authorization, the repository, branch head, destination and action identity. Check the destination after an interrupted action before any replay. Missing access or permission leaves the external action blocked and the content available locally. Draft-only permission permits a draft, never readiness, push, merge or comments.\\n\\n**Worktree.** Work from a git worktree off main. Subagents inherit it. Multiple independent workers on the same branch each get their own isolated worktree. Preserve unrelated dirty work before creating an authorized fresh worktree. Missing independent workers permits an authorized sequential reduction, never a claim of independent review.\\n\\n**Commits.** Commit liberally within the authorized local scope. Rebase into small, ordered commits before opening PRs. Each commit is a future PR: landable, ordered to tell the story. Amend when the fix belongs in a just-made commit. New commit when separable.\\n\\n**PRs.** Run `/deslop` over the diff before commit if that external skill is exposed and authorized. It is not bundled here. Write every PR title, PR description, and commit body with `/technical-writing` through [technical-writing](../../technical-writing/SKILL.md), then apply `/unslop` through [unslop](../../unslop/SKILL.md). Apply every technical-writing layer except Diátaxis. Use one word for each action, keep articles, and avoid `-ing` when a plain verb works.\\n\\n**Titles.** Use Conventional Commits in the form `type(scope): subject`. Use `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, or `perf` as the type. Use the changed area, such as `pstack` or `poteto-mode`, as the scope. Keep the subject short and imperative. Name a real symbol when one carries the change. For example, `fix(pstack): retarget opening-a-pr babysit trigger`. Do not add a trailing period.\\n\\n**Descriptions.** The PR body is a briefing, not the lab notebook. A reviewer who has the diff should learn why the change exists, what it leaves out, what it could break, and how you proved it works, in under a minute. Write short, simple sentences with few identifiers. Do not write walls of text. The squash commit body is the PR body. If the body would make the squash commit longer than about 40 lines, cut the body.\\n\\nPut each section under a `##` heading, not a bold lead-in, so the sections stand apart. Use these sections in order. Drop a section when it has nothing to say.\\n\\n- `## Why` gives the problem and the approach in one to three short sentences. Do not list SHAs or rebase genealogy. Do not add a \\\"based on main\\\" preamble.\\n- `## What changed` has one to three short bullets. Name a real symbol or path only when it carries the change. Name both sides of a rename or retarget.\\n- `## Scope` always names what the PR covers and what it deliberately leaves out, for example a related follow-up or a known gap. Use one to three short items. Do not list symbols or paths, and do not write a file-by-file essay.\\n- `## Tradeoffs` names only rejected alternatives that a reviewer would otherwise ask about. Skip this section when there was no real choice.\\n- `## Blast Radius` gives one or two sentences on who or what the change touches and why that is safe or risky. For a performance change, report one primary number with its unit in `before → after` form. Link the arena or swarm directory for the remaining evidence. Do not include sample-size methodology, swarm recitals, or metric tables.\\n\\nAfter these sections, attach videos or screenshots when they prove a claim. Do not paste full SHAs, swarm or arena lane recitals, lever-correction essays, file-by-file checklists, or \\\"CLEAN\\\" verdicts. Put these details in a linked artifact. A commit body does not restate its subject.\\n\\n**Forge.** Resolve the forge before the first PR operation and keep that choice for create, edit, view, watch, and merge. GitHub CLI (`gh`) is the default. If `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository, prefer `origin pr ...`. If Origin is absent or cannot resolve the repository, stay on `gh` and record the fallback. Do not require Graphite (`gt`).\\n\\n**Built-in PR tool.** When the run provides a built-in PR tool, create, edit, retarget, and mark ready through it, never through a forge CLI. Its exposed instructions define the actual interface. An unavailable, denied or failed tool is a stated blocker, not permission to bypass its tracking through a CLI. A PR made with the CLI misses what the tool tracks, such as a description later runs can edit. Use the resolved forge for everything the tool does not cover, and for every PR operation when the run has no such tool.\\n\\n**Size and stacks.** Prefer five narrow PRs to one large PR. A stack is a base-branch chain. The root PR targets trunk. Each child branch rebases onto its parent's exact tip and its PR targets the parent branch. Without a built-in PR tool, create a child with `origin pr create --status open --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr create --base <parent-branch>` according to the resolved forge, and retarget an existing child with `origin pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>`. Branch from trunk only for independent work. Rebase on trunk before substantial stack work.\\n\\n**Readiness.** The source workflow opens every PR ready, never as a draft, when readiness is explicitly authorized. If only draft creation is authorized, preserve that limit and create a draft through the exposed tool or `gh pr create --draft`. Verify the actual draft state and report the readiness gate open. Use Origin draft creation only when its current interface supports it. Otherwise report blocked. All readiness instructions below require readiness authorization. A built-in PR tool can default to draft, so use its observed ready-creation interface, such as `draft: false` only when that field is actually supported. With Origin, pass `--status open`. With `gh`, omit `--draft`. If a PR still opens as a draft, mark it ready through the PR tool, or run `origin pr ready <number>` or `gh pr ready <number>` according to the resolved forge. Push back when feedback drifts from intent.\\n\\nA subagent that opens a PR runs `interrogate` through [interrogate](../../interrogate/SKILL.md), `/deslop`, and `/no-comments`, and posts the URL. Then it returns to the parent without babysitting, unless it is an Autopilot-full or Autopilot-stack owner. That owner's brief assigns the babysit loop and is the ask [babysit](babysit.md) waits for. The rules here and in [babysit](babysit.md) that hold babysitting until a whole stack is built do not apply to that owner.\\n\\nFor the owner exception, read [Autopilot-full](autopilot-full.md) or [Autopilot-stack](autopilot-stack.md) and the [Bugbot triage rubric](../references/bugbot-triage.md). No watcher, bootstrap or orchestration helper runs in this opening step. Explains subsystem architecture, runtime flow, onboarding mental models. Use why for motivation.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# How\\n\\nExplore the codebase to answer \\\"how does X work?\\\" questions. Produce architectural explanations at the level of a senior engineer onboarding onto a subsystem, enough to build a working mental model, not so much that it reads like annotated source code.\\n\\nBefore dispatch, read [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Bind worker operations to tools actually exposed and authorized in this session. Request the inherited parent model and effort unless a supported explicit selection is observed. Retain rejections and disclose replacements; an unavailable required selection is blocked. Record requested and observed selections separately, using unknown for unobserved values.\\n\\nKeep explorers and explainers read-only. Worker assignments record their role, distinct angle, exact input revision, identity and inspected results under the assignment contract. Reading a prompt does not register a worker. If independent workers are unavailable or unauthorized, disclose reduced capability and perform the same exploration and explanation roles sequentially. Never claim parallel or independent exploration from sequential work. If source access is unavailable or denied, report the gap and limit the explanation to inspected evidence.\\n\\n## Step 1. Assess Complexity\\n\\nIf the scope is ambiguous, state your interpretation and explore. The user can redirect.\\n\\n- **Simple** (a single module, a small utility, a narrow question such as \\\"how does function X work\\\"): no explorers. If workers are unavailable, explore those distinct angles sequentially and retain separate findings. Then go to Step 3.\\n\\n## Step 2b. Direct Explain (simple questions)\\n\\nAssign one explainer worker that explores and explains in one pass:\\n\\n- Role: how explainer\\n- Model and effort: follow the model-role contract\\n- Access: read-only\\n\\nBuild its prompt from `references/explainer-prompt.md` without the explorer-findings section. Fill in the placeholders.\\n\\n---\\n\\nYou are exploring a codebase to understand how something works. Gather facts. Trace code paths, read implementations, map components. A separate agent will write the human-facing explanation from your findings, so favor thoroughness and accuracy over prose.\\n\\nWhen independent workers are available, other explorers investigate different slices in parallel. In reduced capability, the coordinator explores distinct slices sequentially and discloses that limit. Don't try to cover everything. Focus on your assigned angle and go deep.\\n\\n## Question\\n\\n> {QUESTION}\\n\\n## Your Exploration Angle\\n\\n{EXPLORATION_ANGLE}\\n\\n## Exploration Instructions\\n\\nStart by finding the relevant code. Use available file discovery, symbol search and file-reading tools to understand the actual implementation. Don't guess from names. Read the code.\\n\\nFollow this pattern:\\n1. **Find the entry point.** What triggers this behavior? A user action, an API call, a scheduled job? Find where it starts.\\n2. **Trace the flow.** Follow the call chain from the entry point. Read each function. Understand what data flows through and how it transforms.\\n3. **Map the key abstractions.** What types, interfaces, services, or classes are central? Read their definitions. Understand what they represent and why they exist.\\n4. **Find the boundaries.** Where does this subsystem interface with others? What goes in, what comes out?\\n5. **Look for the non-obvious.** Anything surprising? Anything that looks like a historical artifact? Be factual and specific. Reference exact file paths, function names, type names, and line numbers where relevant.\\n\\n### Components Found\\nThe key types, services, classes, and abstractions. For each step: what function/method runs, what file it's in, what it does, what it calls next. Include the data that flows between steps.\\n\\n### Files Read\\nEvery file you read during exploration, so the explainer can reference them.\\n\\n### Boundaries\\nWhere this subsystem connects to other parts of the codebase. The inputs and outputs.\\n\\n### Non-Obvious Things\\nAnything surprising, historically motivated, or easy to get wrong. Things that look like they should work one way but work another.\\n\\n### Open Questions\\nAnything you couldn't fully trace or understand. Be honest about gaps.\\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"path\": \"fixtures/durable-04/bounded-improvement/read-4.txt\",\n      \"originalExternalPath\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-evaluation-20261016/fixtures/durable-04/bounded-improvement/read-4.txt\",\n      \"sha256\": \"08618881df380b5c74a030d6a577fd07f0fc6a3a91b4d0ec1795da3c6350c9b1\",\n      \"bytes\": 3411,\n      \"owners\": [\n        \"grades-native-durable-04.json#1\"\n      ],\n      \"text\": \"# Explainer Prompt Template\\n\\nBuild the explainer worker's prompt from this template. Fill in the placeholders.\\n\\n---\\n\\nYou are writing an architectural explanation for a senior engineer. For complex questions, explorers have traced different slices and gathered findings, independently when supported or sequentially with an explicit reduced-capability disclosure. For simple questions, omit Explorer Findings and explore the source yourself in this role. Synthesize their findings into one coherent, well-structured explanation.\\n\\n## Original Question\\n\\n> {QUESTION}\\n\\n## Explorer Findings\\n\\n{EXPLORER_FINDINGS_ALL}\\n\\n## Instructions\\n\\nThe explorers each investigated a different angle of the same subsystem. Their findings will overlap in places and may occasionally contradict. Reconcile them. Merge overlapping descriptions, resolve contradictions by checking the code yourself, and combine the separate slices into a unified picture.\\n\\nWrite an explanation a senior engineer unfamiliar with this area could read and walk away with a solid mental model, understanding the architecture well enough to start working in it confidently.\\n\\nYou have read-only access to the codebase to check anything, clarify a detail, or fill a gap. Use available file reading, symbol search and file discovery as needed. When explorer findings are supplied, you should not need to re-explore from scratch. Without them, trace entry points, calls, data, abstractions and boundaries yourself; disclose anything you cannot trace.\\n\\n## Output Format\\n\\nUse this structure, adapted to what makes sense for the question. Not every section is needed for every question.\\n\\n### Overview\\n1-2 paragraphs. What is this thing, what does it do, why does it exist. Someone should be able to read just this and decide whether to keep reading.\\n\\n### Key Concepts\\nThe important types, services, or abstractions needed to follow the rest. Brief definitions, not exhaustive.\\n\\n### How It Works\\nThe core of the explanation, and the longest section. Walk through the flow: what triggers it, what happens step by step, where data goes, what the decision points are.\\n\\nUse prose, not pseudocode. Reference specific files and functions so the reader knows where to look, but don't dump large code blocks unless a snippet is essential to a point.\\n\\nWhen the flow involves multiple components talking to each other, or data transforming through stages, include a diagram. Use mermaid (```mermaid) for structured flows (sequence diagrams, flowcharts, component graphs) or ASCII art for simpler relationships where mermaid would be overkill. Use your judgment. A diagram should clarify, not decorate. If prose covers the flow, skip the diagram.\\n\\n### Where Things Live\\nA brief file/directory map. Just the ones someone would need to start working here.\\n\\n### Gotchas\\nNon-obvious things, surprising behavior, historical context, pitfalls. Skip this section if there's nothing worth calling out.\\n\\n## Communication Style\\n\\n- Use concrete language, not abstractions-about-abstractions\\n- Say \\\"the `UserService` calls `AuthClient.refresh()`\\\" not \\\"the service delegates to the client\\\"\\n- When something is complex, explain why it's complex. Don't just describe the complexity\\n- When something is simple, don't pad it out\\n- If there's a helpful analogy, use it. If there isn't, don't force one\\n- If the explorers flagged open questions or gaps, acknowledge them rather than hiding them\\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"path\": \"fixtures/durable-04/bounded-improvement/read-5.txt\",\n      \"originalExternalPath\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-evaluation-20261016/fixtures/durable-04/bounded-improvement/read-5.txt\",\n      \"sha256\": \"81ecaa398ff10882a1e1050c529c04c3a678eecc03e36ad24549379c3776d106\",\n      \"bytes\": 6476,\n      \"owners\": [\n        \"grades-native-durable-04.json#1\"\n      ],\n      \"text\": \"---\\nname: benchmark-checklist\\ndescription: \\\"Vet a perf measurement (limiter, tuning, limits, errors, repeatability, relevance, and whether the work happened) before you report or act on it. Use when you run a benchmark or report a speedup or regression you measured.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Benchmark checklist\\n\\nUse this when you produce a performance number: a PR's before and after, a regression claim, a hillclimb harness, or a library or config choice. [Explain the Number](../principle-explain-the-number/SKILL.md) says why. Answer each question below with evidence from a run, not from a guess about the code.\\n\\nFor a quick ballpark the user asked for, one run is enough. Still check questions 4 and 7, and say that it is one run. Skip the rest unless that run looks wrong. A choice between options is never a ballpark.\\n\\n## Capability and permission checks\\n\\nUse [host-capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to check available inspection, execution, profiling and evidence storage before a run. Use commands only when exposed and authorized. The commands below are examples for compatible systems; use an available platform equivalent when a command is missing. Do not install profilers or stop unrelated processes without authorization. If a check is unavailable, name it and retain the report gates below. Reviewing supplied artifacts can produce a reduced assessment, but cannot supply missing run evidence. If neither artifacts nor authorized inspection are available, report the measurement as blocked.\\n\\nRecord the workload, data size, concurrency, timed region, exact revisions and configurations of every side, and sample count with the run evidence. Check machine contention, tuning, caches, warmup, errors and completed work before claiming a measured improvement. Preserve `disable-model-invocation: true` as source metadata without assuming the host enforces it.\\n\\n## Before you run anything\\n\\n- Write down the claim you expect to make, in the words you would ship (\\\"export is 30% faster at p50 on the 60k-row dataset\\\"). The questions test that sentence.\\n- Read the measurement script. Note what it times, what it counts, and what it ignores.\\n- Check the load average with `uptime` and the core count with `nproc`. If the machine is busy, find out what is running. If you cannot stop it, interleave the sides so both see the same noise, and say so in the report.\\n\\n## The questions\\n\\n1. **Why not double?** Name the limiter. Profile in a run you do not report, because profilers and tracers slow the work down. Use CPU per process (`top`, `pidstat`), a profiler for the runtime (`node --cpu-prof`, `py-spy`, `perf`), I/O wait, and syscall counts (`strace -c` on Linux). Then map the hot spot to source. Watch the load generator too. If it saturates first, you measured the load generator. If a change did not move the number, the limiter explains why, so find it before you call the change useless.\\n2. **Was it tuned?** Run every side the way production runs it: release builds, production flags and env, batching and transaction settings, connection pools, caches as warm or cold as production sees them, and the same versions and data. If one side runs on defaults, you compared configurations, not implementations. A limiter that is a setting, such as a commit per row, a debug build, or a missing index, means that side is untuned. Tune it and measure again before you pick a winner. If you cannot tune it, do not pick a winner from that run. Narrowing the claim to the code as it ships today does not fix this when the user is choosing what to adopt, because they adopt the option, not today's settings.\\n3. **Did it break limits?** Do the arithmetic. Compare bytes per second with disk and network bandwidth, and operations per second times the cost per operation with the cores you have. Compare the time saved with the time the changed piece took. Removing a piece that takes 10% of the run can make the run at most about 11% faster. A result past a limit means the run measured something other than the work, such as a cache, a no-op, or a bug.\\n4. **Did it error?** Count failures and non-success responses, and check that the outputs are correct, not just present. Errors behave differently from successes. Rejections are often fast, and timeouts and retries are slow. If the script does not count errors, add the count.\\n5. **Does it reproduce?** Run each side at least 5 times, and alternate the sides (A, B, A, B, and so on) so that warmup, lazy initialization, caches, and drift do not favor one side. Report the median and the range. Treat a gap smaller than the run-to-run variation as no measurable difference. When the call is close, use a rank-sum test or the harness's own statistics.\\n6. **Does it matter?** Next to any micro result, measure the end-to-end path a user waits on, with realistic data sizes and concurrency. Report the micro result as a share of the whole. A helper that takes 1% of a request can make the request at most 1% faster, however fast the helper gets.\\n7. **Did it even happen?** Confirm the work ran inside the timed region. The request reached the server, the rows were written, the bytes were read, and the code used the result. Lazy code (generators nobody iterates, promises nobody awaits, results the JIT can discard) and timeouts all produce numbers for work that never happened.\\n\\n## Report\\n\\n- Lead with the verdict: faster, slower, no measurable difference, or inconclusive.\\n- Give the number with its unit, the run count, the range, and the limiter. For example, \\\"p50 41 ms → 33 ms, median of 7 runs per side, range 32 to 35 ms after, bound by JSON parsing on one core.\\\"\\n- Call the verdict inconclusive when you claim a difference but cannot name the limiter, when a side ran untuned, or when you could not check questions 4 and 7. Name the gap.\\n- Keep a PR body to one primary number, per the **Opening a PR** playbook. Put the runs, the range, and the limiter evidence in a linked artifact or a notes file.\\n\\n## How this fits the other perf material\\n\\n- The **Perf issue** playbook finds and fixes slowness, and the performance mantras in its step 2 generate the fixes. This skill vets its baseline before the playbook plans from it, and every number after that.\\n- The **Hillclimb** playbook loops on one metric. This skill vets its harness before the harness is frozen. The frozen harness then prints error and work counts, so each keep-or-revert checks questions 4 and 7 for free.\\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"path\": \"fixtures/durable-04/bounded-improvement/read-6.txt\",\n      \"originalExternalPath\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-evaluation-20261016/fixtures/durable-04/bounded-improvement/read-6.txt\",\n      \"sha256\": \"c40999b0f55ca55f74c06ddad12acfd6c022c23a26d9ac4372a3fa332987f4a5\",\n      \"bytes\": 2590,\n      \"owners\": [\n        \"grades-native-durable-04.json#1\"\n      ],\n      \"text\": \"---\\nname: principle-explain-the-number\\ndescription: \\\"Apply before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Explain the Number\\n\\nA measured number is a claim about a system. Before you trust it, report it, or act on it, find what limits it and rule out that it measured something else.\\n\\n**Why:** A run that went wrong still prints a plausible number. Requests that failed, a cache that skipped the work, code that never ran, a side left on default settings, and run-to-run noise all produce results that look fine. If you cannot say why the number is not twice as good, you do not know what you measured.\\n\\n**Pattern:**\\n\\n- **Ask \\\"why not double?\\\"** Name the resource or code path that bounds the result, such as a core, a lock, the disk, the network, or the load generator itself. Get it from a profile or from system counters taken during a run, then map it to source. A guess from reading the code is not a limiter.\\n- **List what else the number could be measuring, and rule out each one with evidence.** The usual suspects are errors, skipped or cached work, an untuned side, noise, and a piece too small to matter end to end.\\n- **Keep the evidence with the number.** Put the run count, the spread, and the limiter in the notes or a linked artifact, so a reader can check the claim.\\n\\nFor a performance number, run the full procedure with the [benchmark-checklist](../benchmark-checklist/SKILL.md) skill. For an eval result, ask the same of the trials: did every run do the task, does the gap hold across trials and models, and does the scenario matter.\\n\\nYou skipped this when the evidence behind a number has no run count, no spread, or no named limiter, or when the time saved is larger than the time the changed piece took.\\n\\nDistinct from [Prove It Works](../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md), which checks that an output is real. This checks that a measured number means what you say it means.\\n\\n## Session capabilities\\n\\nUse [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to check available inspection, execution and evidence storage within the authorized scope. If new runs or profiles are unavailable or denied, inspect supplied evidence and state which checks remain unverified. Do not guess a limiter from source or report an unsupported speedup. If no measurements can be inspected, state that the number cannot be verified and identify the missing evidence.\\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"path\": \"fixtures/durable-04/bounded-improvement/read-7.txt\",\n      \"originalExternalPath\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-evaluation-20261016/fixtures/durable-04/bounded-improvement/read-7.txt\",\n      \"sha256\": \"3c4f05ffecc162b6ae376b7adcf4e7d030c8dfc65a7f26f8519f2c1544c3b98b\",\n      \"bytes\": 8456,\n      \"owners\": [\n        \"grades-native-durable-04.json#1\"\n      ],\n      \"text\": \"---\\nname: show-me-your-work\\ndescription: \\\"Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work: a TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result). Local by default; commit it when a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for /show-me-your-work, autonomous or multi-phase runs, or work a human reviews after stepping away.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Show me your work\\n\\nKeep one canonical log.\\n\\n## The format\\n\\nA single TSV file, one row per decision. Cells stay single-line. Evidence is a pointer, not prose.\\n\\nCopy [references/decision-log-template.tsv](references/decision-log-template.tsv) (the header row) to start a clean log. Columns:\\n\\n- **ts.** ISO8601 timestamp.\\n- **phase.** The phase or workstream.\\n- **decision.** What was chosen or done, one line.\\n- **why.** The reason in plain words. If a principle drove it, say it plainly, not as a jargon tag.\\n- **evidence.** A link or path that proves it: commit SHA, PR number, `file:line`, or an artifact, trace, or screenshot path. Never a paragraph.\\n- **result.** The outcome or predicate state: `tests green`, `reverted`, `pixel-diff 0`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `open`.\\n\\nAn example, plain-spoken so a reviewer reads it at a glance.\\n\\n```\\nts\\tphase\\tdecision\\twhy\\tevidence\\tresult\\n2026-05-24T09:02:00Z\\tframe\\tcounted the work first, about 100 components and roughly 75 hours\\twanted to know the size before starting a long run\\tcommit 3a9f1c2\\tfound 5 things to sort out before starting\\n2026-05-24T09:40:00Z\\tharness\\ttook screenshots of the old version before changing anything\\tso we can compare old against new and catch any visual change\\tscripts/snapshot.sh, baseline/\\tsaved 120 reference screenshots\\n2026-05-24T11:15:00Z\\twidget\\tmoved the widget styles over without changing how it looks\\tkeep the change small and the result identical\\tcommit 7c21e0a, pixel-diff 0\\tlooks identical, tests pass\\n2026-05-24T12:30:00Z\\twidget\\tthrew out a helper's work because its screenshots were blank\\tchecked the real files instead of trusting its summary\\tworktree reset\\treverted, tightened the instructions for next time\\n```\\n\\n## Logging a row\\n\\nWrite each entry the way you'd tell a teammate what you did. Plain words, concrete actions, no AI speak or abstract jargon (the **unslop** skill applies to log text too).\\n\\nUse the helper [scripts/log.sh](scripts/log.sh) with `<logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>` through an authorized execution binding. Pass an explicit nonempty local output path that this task owns. The helper rejects tabs, newlines and carriage returns in any argument before creating directories or writing bytes. It stamps `ts`, writes the header on first use, preserves previous rows, and prefixes any cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` with a single quote. Use this helper for generated or user-supplied cells so validation and formula protection apply consistently. Host execution still requires an authorized binding.\\n\\nLog decision points and checkpoints, not every action: a fork chosen, a unit completed with its verification result, a pivot or revert with its trigger, a blocker surfaced, a gate fixed. For loop runs, one row per iteration. Skip the trivial and self-evident.\\n\\nA run is one agent conversation, including its later turns and any summary of it. A pickup, a replacement agent, or a new chat starts a new run. When a run adds to a log that already has rows, its first row has phase `start`, and so does its first row after another run's `start` row. So a run that comes back to a log in a later turn first reads the log's last rows to see whether another run wrote since. A `start` row names the `ts` range of the rows before it that this run did not write, and its evidence names this run, such as its agent id. Use phase `start` for nothing else.\\n\\n## Where it lives\\n\\nBy default the log is a working artifact, not committed. Keep it at `decisions.tsv` in the work dir, or `.audit/<task-slug>.tsv` when several efforts run at once, and leave it out of git.\\n\\nCommit it only when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result.\\n\\n## Rules\\n\\n- Append-only. A wrong call gets a new row that supersedes it. Never edit or delete history.\\n- Prefer evidence produced by committed scripts over hand-made one-offs (the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill).\\n\\n## Audit the log against the transcript\\n\\nAt the end of the run, before handing back, check the log told the truth. Discover this run's transcript through the current session's history binding, or an explicitly identified transcript in the active workspace. The source used `agent-transcripts/`; do not assume the host provides that directory. Never search unrelated private chats or global transcript directories. If this run's transcript is inaccessible or incomplete, record the gap and do not claim a complete transcript audit. Walk this run's rows against what actually happened. Each stretch of them begins at one of this run's `start` rows, or at the first row if this run created the log, and ends at the next `start` row of another run:\\n\\n- Check that every row maps to a real decision or action.\\n- Check that each row's evidence resolves and shows what the row claims.\\n- A fork, pivot, or abandoned approach that shaped the work but isn't logged is a gap. Add it.\\n\\nCorrect the log, not the story. The audit never edits or removes a row, even an invented one. When a row records neither a real decision nor a real action, or its claim or evidence is wrong, add a row that supersedes it with what actually happened and a pointer that resolves. This audit does not check rows outside this run's stretches. If this run's own work shows one of them is wrong, supersede it like any wrong call.\\n\\n## Cross-model review of the trail\\n\\nBefore handing back, use an authorized exposed independent-worker binding to request a reviewer on a different model family from the one that did the work. Follow [model selection](../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Observe the worker identity, result and actual model family before claiming independent cross-model review. If no authorized worker or verified different family is available, record that review as blocked. An authorized sequential scan is reduced capability and does not satisfy this review requirement. Self-review is not a substitute. The subagent reads the audit trail and the run's transcript, then flags what the user should pay attention to. Not a redo of the work, a scan for what's suboptimal or risky.\\n\\n- Decisions logged with weak or absent evidence.\\n- Verification steps skipped or claimed without proof in the transcript.\\n- Choices that look risky in hindsight (premature, scope-creeping, papering over a symptom).\\n- Gaps the user would otherwise miss on a casual skim.\\n\\nEvery reply for a run that produced a trail ends with an \\\"Attention\\\" section. Lead with the reviewer's model on its own line (`reviewed by <model>`), then list each flag pointing to specific rows or moments. \\\"No flags\\\" is a valid value. The model name is not.\\n\\n## Reviewing the trail\\n\\nRead top to bottom, follow the evidence pointers, spot-check. GitHub renders a committed TSV as a table. `column -s$'\\\\t' -t decisions.tsv` renders it in a terminal.\\n\\n## Composing this skill\\n\\nOther skills route their audit trail here instead of inventing one. Reference it by name and let it own the format. Don't restate the columns.\\n\\n## Host capabilities and safety\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) for history, execution, persistence and reviewer bindings. Write only to an authorized local path, then read back the saved trail before claiming persistence. A log is evidence of recorded decisions, not proof of unattended execution or recovery. Do not include credentials, tokens, raw secret-bearing output or unrelated private data. Use a safe evidence pointer or a redacted local artifact instead. Record only observed results; unresolved predicates stay `open` or `INCONCLUSIVE`.\\n\\nThe default local trail does not authorize a commit. Commit, publish, message or other external action requires explicit authorization. Preserve append-only history and scope every transcript audit to this run. When review is blocked, keep the Attention section and state `reviewed by unknown` if no actual reviewer model was observed, followed by the capability gap. Never use `No flags` to imply an unperformed review.\\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"path\": \"fixtures/durable-04/bounded-improvement/read-8.txt\",\n      \"originalExternalPath\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-evaluation-20261016/fixtures/durable-04/bounded-improvement/read-8.txt\",\n      \"sha256\": \"fb47611cbb75ea17aa80cb4f8dbfc7978b8844450b0ce702961bdef65cbb1342\",\n      \"bytes\": 1717,\n      \"owners\": [\n        \"grades-native-durable-04.json#1\"\n      ],\n      \"text\": \"#!/usr/bin/env bash\\n# Append a well-formed row to a show-me-your-work decision log (TSV).\\n# Usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\nset -euo pipefail\\n\\nif [ \\\"$#\\\" -ne 6 ]; then\\n\\tprintf 'usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\\\n' >&2\\n\\texit 1\\nfi\\n\\n# The caller owns the output path.
