Plan, review, verify the numbers. Tie every fix to a measurement, don't read source instead of measuring.\\n\\nRead the complete [poteto mode](../SKILL.md) and required leaves. Use [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md), the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md) and the full [poteto role prompt](../../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md). Record actual exposed controls, execution and artifact access before using them. Missing required reads stop dependent work. Do not install controls or profilers implicitly.\\n\\n1. Capture a baseline trace via the matching control skill. Discover the actual control-cli or control-ui companion and its exposed tools for the measured CLI, UI or runtime. Missing or denied matching controls leave capture blocked. Reviewing supplied traces is a reduced assessment and does not prove a new capture. Vet the baseline, and each later number, with the complete [benchmark-checklist](../../benchmark-checklist/SKILL.md) and its [explain-the-number](../../principle-explain-the-number/SKILL.md) contract. Record the exact baseline and treatment revisions, workload, data size, concurrency, timed region, configuration, tuning, cache state, warmup, sample count, errors and completed work. Keep comparable runs and their artifacts. A choice between fixes is not the checklist's one-run ballpark exception.\\n2. Run [how](../../how/SKILL.md) to ground hypotheses. Don't claim a perf ceiling without running it first.\\n   Try the performance mantras in order, cheapest first:\\n   1. Don't do it. Stop work whose result nothing uses rather than cheapening it.\\n   2. Do it, but don't do it again.\\n   3. Do it less.\\n   4. Do it later.\\n   5. Do it when they're not looking.\\n   6. Do it concurrently.\\n   7. Do it cheaper.\\n\\n   When an earlier mantra meets the target, stop.\\n3. Plan the fix from the trace. If it crosses a function boundary, run the complete [architect](../../architect/SKILL.md) workflow first, including its runner prompts, candidate screening and rationale. Delegate implementation to an authorized independent worker with the complete poteto role prompt, an exact input revision and distinct owned output. Use the configured perf-issue role only when its model and effort are supported by current exposed operations. Otherwise request inherited selection and disclose rejected or unavailable selections. Record requested and observed values separately; unknown observed values prove no model diversity. If the exact selection is required but unavailable, block it. Inspect the returned artifacts and review the diff. Without authorized workers, perform authorized sequential implementation as reduced capability; independent delegation remains unsatisfied. Capture a post-fix trace on the matching measured system and vet it with the same checklist.\\n   Apply [sequence-verifiable-units](../../principle-sequence-verifiable-units/SKILL.md), verifying each attempt before trying the next. An unavailable check blocks advancement and stays unverified.\\n4. Parse and compare the artifacts, including JSON to sqlite and a diff when applicable, using available authorized execution and storage. Retain original traces and the comparison artifact. Apply all seven checklist questions. For a comparison, run each side at least five times, alternate the sides, report median and range, and treat a gap smaller than variation as no measurable difference. Keep profiling runs separate from reported timings. Name the limiter from run evidence, check physical limits, production tuning, correct outputs, error counts, actual completed work and end-to-end relevance. \\\"Inconclusive\\\" or wrong-surface is not a pass. Flag it. Missing limiter, an untuned side, or unchecked errors or completed work makes a claimed difference inconclusive. Incompatible workloads, revisions or configurations cannot support the proposed performance claim.\\n5. Cite the measurement in the PR. Keep one primary number with its unit in the body and link the runs, range, limiter and trace comparison artifact. Prepare a local draft when PR writes are unauthorized; do not claim that draft is a created PR.\\n6. Hillclimb and Opening a PR remain pending companion dependencies for tasks 18 and 21, with task 24 integration.\\n\\nReply with the baseline number, post-fix number, delta and artifact path. Define done, then drive to it while execution is available. This is the playbook for \\\"run until done\\\" and \\\"/loop until X\\\". The source's /loop was a host built-in, not a pstack skill or a portable tool binding.\\n\\nRead [poteto-mode](../SKILL.md) in full. Discover actual operations through [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md) and follow the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Upstream autonomy does not override user gates or host permissions.\\n\\n1. State the exit condition as a checkable predicate before the first iteration, such as tests green, repro fixed, all N PRs merged or pixel-diff zero. Record the check and its current evidence. A merge predicate does not authorize merging.\\n2. Pick an exposed, authorized wake mechanism and observe its registration before claiming it active. An event to watch, such as CI, a merge or a ref advancing, gets an independent watcher worker with a long time-based heartbeat as fallback. No event gets a fixed-interval heartbeat sized to when the result is worth re-checking. Use the [poteto role prompt](../../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md), exact assignment revision and isolated outputs for a watcher. Follow [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md), defaulting to inherit-parent and recording actual models only when observed. Record missing or failed wake, heartbeat, worker and stop/control bindings separately. Never install or schedule implicitly. If persistent wake is unavailable, continue useful authorized iterations in the current turn and save the continuation brief below before returning. Label this reduced capability, without a promise of work after the turn. A foreground check is not an independent watcher. If control is unavailable, disclose that limit and do not claim a worker stopped or unattended recovery is safe.\\n3. Each iteration makes the smallest change the evidence justifies and verifies it against the predicate. Commit if it advanced and commit authorization and review gates are satisfied. Otherwise keep the verified change local and report the unmet gate. Discard changes that did not help, reverting only this run's owned changes. Revert speculative fixes that merely \\\"might help\\\". Sequence work through [sequence-verifiable-units](../../principle-sequence-verifiable-units/SKILL.md), verifying each unit before the next instead of batching checks at the end. Missing verification blocks dependent advancement.\\n4. Address mid-run broken skills, related bugs, flaky verifiers, review noise, tooling failures, orphaned follow-ups and fixable drift through poteto-mode within authorization. Put out-of-band fixes in their own PR when PR creation is authorized, using the mode's Opening a PR route. Otherwise prepare the separate local fix and disclose the unperformed PR action. Do not park authorized reversible work for the human or ask a question an experiment can settle. Surface irreversible actions, explicit operator gates, genuine product or preference calls no experiment can settle, or a real dead end. Stop dependent work on a broken contract, continue independent work, and return to the main predicate after each side fix.\\n5. Checkpoint every iteration through [show-me-your-work](../../show-me-your-work/SKILL.md), with what changed and whether the predicate moved. Use its [log helper](../../show-me-your-work/scripts/log.sh) through authorized execution with an explicit owned local log path and its [template](../../show-me-your-work/references/decision-log-template.tsv). Keep append-only history, read back saved records, audit against this run's available transcript and preserve its cross-model review and Attention requirements. Missing history, persistence or independent review remains visible. A saved log does not prove unattended execution.\\n6. Stop successfully only when the predicate is met. A plateau is not completion. Keep going and pivot while authorization and execution permit. Surface a genuine dead end instead of spinning and never relax the predicate to declare victory. A session boundary, unavailable persistent tool or explicit pause requires a handoff with the predicate still open, not a completion claim.\\n\\nWhen ongoing work cannot survive the turn, save a continuation brief at an explicit authorized local path and read it back. Include the unchanged exit predicate and current state, iterations completed, current revision and owned changes, verification commands and results, decision-log path, accepted and discarded changes, outstanding gates and missing capabilities, pending action identities and known outcomes, and the next check or experiment. A new run must inspect current state and permissions before continuing or replaying an action. Unknown external outcomes block replay. If local persistence is denied or unavailable, return the brief inline and state that no durable save occurred. Neither form registers a wake mechanism or proves automatic pickup.\\n\\nReply with the exit condition, iterations run, what landed, what was discarded and final predicate state. Distinguish verified local work from actual commits, PRs and merges. Link the saved trail and continuation brief only after readback. Report missing capabilities, blocked gates and any unperformed action. Keep show-me-your-work's Attention section when a trail was produced.\\n\",\n    \"sha256\": \"d7a61255568f81fb8facddc8d8f5aaa710ce0407569175eccdf7dd050744ba1a\",\n    \"result\": \"read\",\n    \"exit\": 0\n  },\n  {\n    \"path\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/opening-a-pr.md\",\n    \"content\": \"### Opening a PR\\n\\nInvoked at the end of every other playbook.\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [workflow ownership](../../../references/workflow-ownership.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md), and the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md). These documents live at the package root. Prepare a reviewable title, body, verification artifacts, and intended base before any external operation. Record explicit authorization, the repository, branch head, destination and action identity. Check the destination after an interrupted action before any replay. Missing access or permission leaves the external action blocked and the content available locally. Draft-only permission permits a draft, never readiness, push, merge or comments.\\n\\n**Worktree.** Work from a git worktree off main. Subagents inherit it. Multiple independent workers on the same branch each get their own isolated worktree. Preserve unrelated dirty work before creating an authorized fresh worktree. Report a snarled worktree instead of resetting or discarding unowned changes. Missing independent workers permits an authorized sequential reduction, never a claim of independent review.\\n\\n**Commits.** Commit liberally within the authorized local scope. Rebase into small, ordered commits before opening PRs. Each commit is a future PR: landable, ordered to tell the story. Amend when the fix belongs in a just-made commit. New commit when separable.\\n\\n**PRs.** Run `/deslop` over the diff before commit if that external skill is exposed and authorized. It is not bundled here. If absent, disclose the missing slop-strip and leave that gate open and block creation until the required review gate is satisfied; do not install it or treat prose cleanup as equivalent. Run `/no-comments` through [no-comments](../../no-comments/SKILL.md) before review. Write every PR title, PR description, and commit body with `/technical-writing` through [technical-writing](../../technical-writing/SKILL.md), then apply `/unslop` through [unslop](../../unslop/SKILL.md). Apply every technical-writing layer except Diátaxis. Use one word for each action, keep articles, and avoid `-ing` when a plain verb works.\\n\\n**Titles.** Use Conventional Commits in the form `type(scope): subject`. Use `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, or `perf` as the type. Use the changed area, such as `pstack` or `poteto-mode`, as the scope. Keep the subject short and imperative. Name a real symbol when one carries the change. For example, `fix(pstack): retarget opening-a-pr babysit trigger`. Do not add a trailing period.\\n\\n**Descriptions.** The PR body is a briefing, not the lab notebook. A reviewer who has the diff should learn why the change exists, what it leaves out, what it could break, and how you proved it works, in under a minute. Write short, simple sentences with few identifiers. Do not write walls of text. The squash commit body is the PR body. If the body would make the squash commit longer than about 40 lines, cut the body.\\n\\nPut each section under a `##` heading, not a bold lead-in, so the sections stand apart. Use these sections in order. Drop a section when it has nothing to say.\\n\\n- `## Why` gives the problem and the approach in one to three short sentences. Do not list SHAs or rebase genealogy. Do not add a \\\"based on main\\\" preamble.\\n- `## What changed` has one to three short bullets. Name a real symbol or path only when it carries the change. Name both sides of a rename or retarget.\\n- `## Scope` always names what the PR covers and what it deliberately leaves out, for example a related follow-up or a known gap. Use one to three short items. Do not list symbols or paths, and do not write a file-by-file essay.\\n- `## Tradeoffs` names only rejected alternatives that a reviewer would otherwise ask about. Skip this section when there was no real choice.\\n- `## Blast Radius` gives one or two sentences on who or what the change touches and why that is safe or risky. If main is red, state the cost of leaving it red.\\n- `## Verification` has one to three bullets. Each bullet names a real run path and its outcome. For a performance change, report one primary number with its unit in `before → after` form. Link the arena or swarm directory for the remaining evidence. Do not include sample-size methodology, swarm recitals, or metric tables.\\n\\nAfter these sections, attach videos or screenshots when they prove a claim. Do not paste full SHAs, swarm or arena lane recitals, lever-correction essays, file-by-file checklists, or \\\"CLEAN\\\" verdicts. Put these details in a linked artifact. A commit body does not restate its subject.\\n\\n**Forge.** Resolve the forge before the first PR operation and keep that choice for create, edit, view, watch, and merge. GitHub CLI (`gh`) is the default. If `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository, prefer `origin pr ...`. If Origin is absent or cannot resolve the repository, stay on `gh` and record the fallback. Do not require Graphite (`gt`).\\n\\n**Built-in PR tool.** When the run provides a built-in PR tool, create, edit, retarget, and mark ready through it, never through a forge CLI. Its exposed instructions define the actual interface. An unavailable, denied or failed tool is a stated blocker, not permission to bypass its tracking through a CLI. A PR made with the CLI misses what the tool tracks, such as a description later runs can edit. Use the resolved forge for everything the tool does not cover, and for every PR operation when the run has no such tool.\\n\\n**Size and stacks.** Prefer five narrow PRs to one large PR. A stack is a base-branch chain. The root PR targets trunk. Each child branch rebases onto its parent's exact tip and its PR targets the parent branch. Without a built-in PR tool, create a child with `origin pr create --status open --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr create --base <parent-branch>` according to the resolved forge, and retarget an existing child with `origin pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>`. Branch from trunk only for independent work. Rebase on trunk before substantial stack work.\\n\\n**Readiness.** The source workflow opens every PR ready, never as a draft, when readiness is explicitly authorized. If only draft creation is authorized, preserve that limit and create a draft through the exposed tool or `gh pr create --draft`. Verify the actual draft state and report the readiness gate open. Use Origin draft creation only when its current interface supports it. Otherwise report blocked. All readiness instructions below require readiness authorization. A built-in PR tool can default to draft, so use its observed ready-creation interface, such as `draft: false` only when that field is actually supported. With Origin, pass `--status open`. With `gh`, omit `--draft`. If a PR still opens as a draft, mark it ready through the PR tool, or run `origin pr ready <number>` or `gh pr ready <number>` according to the resolved forge. Run `origin pr view <number>` or `gh pr view <number>` before you refer to PR status.\\n\\n**Babysit.** Opening a PR does not start a babysit. Post the URL and keep building. Finish the phase or stack first. Run a separate babysit pass only when the user asks for one after the whole stack exists. A babysit for each new PR stalls the build and spends checks on commits that later waves restart. Push back when feedback drifts from intent.\\n\\nA subagent that opens a PR runs `interrogate` through [interrogate](../../interrogate/SKILL.md), `/deslop`, and `/no-comments`, and posts the URL. Then it returns to the parent without babysitting, unless it is an Autopilot-full or Autopilot-stack owner. That owner's brief assigns the babysit loop and is the ask [babysit](babysit.md) waits for. The owner starts the loop after its code-ready report and reports merge-ready or STACK-READY as its playbook says. The rules here and in [babysit](babysit.md) that hold babysitting until a whole stack is built do not apply to that owner.\\n\\nFor the owner exception, read [Autopilot-full](autopilot-full.md) or [Autopilot-stack](autopilot-stack.md) and the [Bugbot triage rubric](../references/bugbot-triage.md). These briefs assign babysitting only within explicit user authorization and observed capabilities. Opening a PR alone never supplies that authorization. No watcher, bootstrap or orchestration helper runs in this opening step. Babysit owns the actual watcher binding.\\n\",\n    \"sha256\": \"4198f32b22cf1d8ff367deee1dbfea805e6eecdd7ff1da3409ae7c0b07fb1c59\",\n    \"result\": \"read\",\n    \"exit\": 0\n  },\n  {\n    \"path\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md\",\n    \"content\": \"# Poteto agent prompt\\n\\nUse this role for `/poteto-mode` and requests for poteto's style. Supply these instructions to a fresh independent worker for each new task when the session exposes and permits that operation. Resume a worker only in the strict cases named by poteto-mode's Subagents section. Generic worker routing is acceptable only when it carries this entire prompt and the required mode read; otherwise it skips the style contract.\\n\\nBefore any work, read [poteto-mode's SKILL.md](../../skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) in full, including its inline Principles index. Navigate to the leaf `principle-*` skill whenever you apply that principle. If the mode or an applicable leaf is unavailable, report that missing dependency and stop dependent work. Do not reconstruct the mode from a summary.\\n\\nFollow [model roles](../model-roles.md) and [session capabilities](../host-capabilities.md). This prompt does not register an agent or promise background execution. Record requested and observed models separately. Preserve user authorization and host permissions throughout the mode. An authorized sequential fallback uses the same full read and discloses reduced capability; it does not count as an independent worker.\\n\",\n    \"sha256\": \"9839239c6ebc72de8165f8a6fa4a6326fea7293e15a47d24f98396df2a61b3fb\",\n    \"result\": \"read\",\n    \"exit\": 0\n  }\n]"

      "kind": "case-response",
      "text": "# bounded-improvement result\n\nNo performance fix was accepted. Retain repaired baseline bc83cb8963fb770d5ff028fb56d93f9efa2a9b0e. The target remains unmet. This is an observed local experiment with blocked method gates, not a host pass or self-grade.\n\n## Source and task identity\n\nCase ID is bounded-improvement. Source case is docs/parity/cases/playbooks/hillclimb.json. Operative freeze supplied by the user is 51f209daf83cd97d64f89881d66533bb59dc57db. All 20 named exact native 0.1.3 source files were read completely, with bounded rereads repairing truncated mode output. sources.json preserves exact paths, sizes and SHA256 values. The installed cache is not a Git repository, so its freeze identity is user-supplied rather than independently recovered from Git HEAD. The registry role alias agents/poteto-agent.md resolves to the supplied references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md.\n\nActual native task identities and immutable actual-owner assignment records are how-01 with /root/how_identity; candidate-indexed with /root/indexed_identity; candidate-streaming with /root/streaming_identity; candidate-cheap with /root/cheap_identity; judge-01 with /root/judge_identity. Parent /root owns integration, measurement and the canonical trail. Each worker was first bootstrapped for identity only, then received an actual-owner assignment before followup release. Both prepared candidate identities and assignments existed before either candidate completion. The fresh judge was spawned after all completed candidate artifacts and summaries were inspected.\n\nRequested model and effort were inherit-parent. Actual model and effort were not exposed and remain unknown. No configured selection, model diversity or different-family review is claimed. native-worker-events.json captures observed order and returned identities. It is a scoped manual capture of the native conversation, not a complete transcript export. Full original worker command receipts exist for the cheap experiment; the other workers' reports disclose command observations and native transcript limits.\n\n## Checklist ordering failure\n\nThe checklist was saved before source-dependent execution, gates, worker dispatch and measurement, but after initial read-only shell inventory and a memory lookup. The user's stricter requirement was before execution. That gate was not satisfied. checklist-order-correction.md and an append-only correction row supersede the initial checklist's overbroad claim. This cannot be repaired retroactively or converted into a full case pass.\n\n## Actual response and measurements\n\nThe frozen target was at least 10 percent lower median milliseconds for 20 wide CSV calls, plus at least three actual single-hypothesis attempts. Minimum sample count was five alternating baseline/trial runs per comparison. No predicate was relaxed. Scope's 15-minute measurement budget and the user's 25-minute overall budget were retained.\n\nThe actual command is the exact Bun binary recorded in frozen-config.json, with --no-install, metric.mjs, an exact owned copy path, and wide. Same harness SHA256, workload, runtime 1.4.2, concurrency one, five warmups and twenty timed calls were used throughout. metric.mjs retains all results and checks all twenty against independently constructed expected serialization after timing. It counts errors, completed rows, invalid outputs, bytes and hashes. No timings from original measure.mjs are mixed with this metric. Original measure.mjs was read; its final-output-only validation motivated the stronger retained-output script.\n\nImportant validity limit. The timer covers CSV calls and string retention. Equality, hashing and byte counting occur after timing. A concatenated string may defer flattening until consumption. These measurements describe fixture CSV-call duration and cannot prove full consuming export latency, production latency or cross-host comparability. No candidate is accepted on this metric. The frozen metric was not changed mid-campaign to manufacture a gain.\n\n| Hypothesis | Baseline median ms | Baseline range ms | Trial median ms | Trial range ms | Duration reduction | Decision |\n| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |\n| indexed | 201.877 | 200.512 to 211.461 | 201.470 | 198.713 to 203.052 | 0.2017% | Rejected, sparse regression and noise |\n| streaming | 201.630 | 200.289 to 201.777 | 361.579 | 342.046 to 403.868 | -79.3281% | Rejected, sparse regression |\n| cheap | 198.740 | 198.017 to 207.886 | 195.795 | 186.841 to 201.804 | 1.4818% | Unaccepted, noise and no prepared SHA |\n\nThe percentages are calculated as 100 times baseline median minus trial median, divided by baseline median. Negative reduction means greater duration. Concatenation's measured median duration was 79.3281 percent greater, not a claim about production speed or throughput.\n\nAll thirty comparison samples are retained in comparison-indexed.ndjson, comparison-streaming.ndjson and comparison-cheap.ndjson. They recorded 7,200,000 completed rows, 600 validated outputs, zero errors and zero invalid outputs. Every side completed 240,000 rows and validated twenty outputs per sample. All wide fingerprints matched 14931332596500ae2ebb9c865a97fb6de54dd7efd916ca6096b6a164a693d444. Per-comparison summaries retain every sample, median, range and delta. No lucky-only selection occurred.\n\nSensitivity runs actually observed short 4.900875 ms, multiline 21.996667 ms and wide 203.014625 ms on baseline. These single exploratory observations separated workload sizes; they are not treatment wins. Wide has 12,000 rows by sixteen fields; short and multiline have 1,200 and 5,000 rows by four fields. No service history/state or concurrent production workload is represented.\n\nSeparate diagnostic CPU profiles were captured for baseline and all three hypotheses, excluded from timing samples. Local CPU/string-processing work maps to quote and traversal/concatenation in csv.mjs. Whole-process self samples put quote at 48.4 percent for baseline, 50.5 percent for indexed and 45.7 percent for cheap; concatenation csv and quote show 38.4 and 36.9 percent. Setup and validation are also profiled. These percentages do not quantify timed-region savings or prove production tuning. No production configuration or consuming request path is supplied.\n\nActive background load was observed and never stopped. One-minute load ranged 7.619 to 13.040 across thirty samples on fourteen runtime-reported logical cores. ps and sysctl inspection was denied by the sandbox. The runtime supplied CPU count and load values. This is noisy shared-host evidence. Stability and production applicability remain limited.\n\n## Revision and correctness evidence\n\nRoot personally ran the literal Bun correctness gate on separate detached clones at all four supplied SHAs. preparation.ndjson retains commands, returns, order and exit codes. Defective history 0d4d7e3fbad1390658c9d1db7ba3142e55ce4b09 failed with exit 1. Repaired baseline and both proposals passed with exit 0. The original input remains at repaired baseline and clean.\n\nIndexed proposal cb1d14a62014130efba9d4576b1273b1f3b0c6a4 replaces map with indexed preallocated loops. Concatenation proposal 6551c63aa583143c092d9d2438fabeecc5f1c971 appends to a complete in-memory string. Both independently flagged sparse-array hazards. Root reproduced them. Baseline returns an empty field for a sparse cell and an empty row for a sparse outer element. Both proposals emit undefined for the sparse cell and throw for the sparse row. regression-probes.json retains all six outcomes; process exit was 1. Dense fixture gates cannot override this semantic regression.\n\nThe cheap hypothesis preserves map/join and avoids replaceAll when quoted text has no literal quote. Its literal gate and seven probes passed. It was measured with baseline HEAD but uncommitted source SHA256 31ead66bba38c4db86fd11487c5f278b687e4733070a706967449b8f458cf9ea. That is a content fingerprint, not a prepared Git revision. No accepted revision-bound gain is claimed. The worker's initial hashing-driver error and successful receipt-preserving resume are disclosed in cheap-owned/driver-events.json. No timing was manufactured during that failure.\n\nPrepared sample runs checked HEAD each time, but did not hash source cleanliness each time. Workers only inspected those copies, and before/after inspections found clean trees. This is not immutable per-sample tree proof. Cheap samples additionally checked their measured source hash. Root retained cheap's measured bytes at rejected/cheap-csv.mjs and its historical diff, then restored only that completed worker's owned csv.mjs. All selected/input copies remain clean. Prepared candidate artifacts were never integrated and remain exact rejected inputs.\n\nThree hypotheses were measured. Two have prepared exact Git identities; the third is explicitly uncommitted. Zero were kept or integrated; two prepared proposals were rejected from selection; one owned uncommitted edit was fully reverted. No accepted fixes or new commits exist. Final selected revision is the same baseline, so accepted revision change is zero percent. This is an unchanged-code result, not a new equal-latency measurement. The first matched baseline median is 201.877416 ms; its 10 percent target would be 181.689674 ms. No accepted final timing reaches it.\n\n## Variants and stopping rule\n\nvariants.md records each requested variant. The registry role alias agents/poteto-agent.md resolves to the supplied references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md.\n\nActual native task identities and immutable actual-owner assignment records are how-01 with /root/how_identity; candidate-indexed with /root/indexed_identity; candidate-streaming with /root/streaming_identity; candidate-cheap with /root/cheap_identity; judge-01 with /root/judge_identity. This cannot be repaired retroactively or converted into a full case pass.\n\n## Actual response and measurements\n\nThe frozen target was at least 10 percent lower median milliseconds for 20 wide CSV calls, plus at least three actual single-hypothesis attempts.       "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "Input setup commits are preparation only; native workflow MUST NOT commit. Fixed metric: median milliseconds for 20 full CSV exports, lower is better; keep exact workload name unchanged per comparison, five alternating runs minimum each side, same Bun binary/config, warmups and output hashes/errors/completed rows retained. Target 10 percent improvement on wide workload plus minimum 3 actual single-hypothesis attempts; stop only unchanged predicate or explicit marginal-cost/dead-end limit, max foreground budget 15 minutes. Retain lucky/noise/workload-change/regression scenarios honestly as supplied concepts unless actually observed, never manufacture timings. Actual source how, architecture if appropriate, checklist, helper persistence and native isolation/review remain mandatory. No external actions/install.\n"

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import{csv}from'./csv.mjs';import{workload}from'./workloads.mjs';import{createHash}from'node:crypto';const name=process.argv[2];if(!['short','wide','multiline'].includes(name))throw Error('unknown workload');const rows=workload(name);const loops=20;for(let i=0;i<5;i++)csv(rows);const start=performance.now();let text;let errors=0,completed=0;for(let i=0;i<loops;i++){try{text=csv(rows);completed+=rows.length}catch{errors++}}const ms=performance.now()-start;console.log(JSON.stringify({name,loops,rows:rows.length,completed,expectedCompleted:rows.length*loops,errors,bytes:Buffer.byteLength(text??''),sha256:createHash('sha256').update(text??'').digest('hex'),milliseconds:ms}));if(errors||completed!==rows.length*loops)process.exit(1);\n"

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import{readFileSync,writeFileSync}from'node:fs';import{resolve}from'node:path';\nconst out=import.meta.dir,trial=process.argv[2],events=readFileSync(resolve(out,`comparison-${trial}.ndjson`),'utf8').trim().split('\\n').map(JSON.parse);\nconst groups={};for(const e of events){const r=JSON.parse(e.stdout);(groups[e.side]??=[]).push(r);if(e.exitCode!==0||r.errors||r.invalidOutputs||r.completed!==240000||r.validatedOutputs!==20)throw Error('invalid run');}\nconst stats={};for(const [side,runs]of Object.entries(groups)){const values=runs.map(r=>r.milliseconds),s=[...values].sort((a,b)=>a-b);stats[side]={values,median:s[Math.floor(s.length/2)],min:s[0],max:s.at(-1),range:s.at(-1)-s[0],samples:s.length,errors:runs.reduce((s,r)=>s+r.errors,0),completed:runs.reduce((s,r)=>s+r.completed,0),validatedOutputs:runs.reduce((s,r)=>s+r.validatedOutputs,0),hashes:[...new Set(runs.map(r=>r.sha256))]};}\nconst b=stats.baseline,t=stats[trial];const delta=b.median-t.median;const result={trial,stats,deltaMilliseconds:delta,percentReduction:100*delta/b.median,beyondConservativeRange:delta>Math.max(b.range,t.range),verdict:trial==='cheap'?'UNACCEPTED uncommitted experiment; no prepared revision-bound gain':'REJECTED for sparse semantic regression; fixture timing cannot override correctness',noiseVerdict:Math.abs(delta)<=Math.max(b.range,t.range)?'gap smaller than observed range':'gap exceeds individual ranges; still no acceptance',firstPairPercentReduction:100*(b.values[0]-t.values[0])/b.values[0]};writeFileSync(resolve(out,`summary-${trial}.json`),JSON.stringify(result,null,2));console.log(JSON.stringify(result,null,2));\n"

      "text": "No gain was accepted. Baseline `bc83cb8963fb770d5ff028fb56d93f9efa2a9b0e` remains selected, with 0% accepted change.       "text": "import{readFileSync,writeFileSync}from'node:fs';import{resolve}from'node:path';\nconst out=import.meta.dir,events=['indexed','streaming','cheap'].flatMap(n=>readFileSync(resolve(out,`comparison-${n}.ndjson`),'utf8').trim().split('\\n').map(JSON.parse));\nconst loads=events.flatMap(e=>[e.before.load[0],e.after.load[0]]),work=events.map(e=>JSON.parse(e.stdout));\nconst summary={samples:events.length,totalCompletedRows:work.reduce((s,r)=>s+r.completed,0),totalValidatedOutputs:work.reduce((s,r)=>s+r.validatedOutputs,0),errors:work.reduce((s,r)=>s+r.errors,0),invalidOutputs:work.reduce((s,r)=>s+r.invalidOutputs,0),oneMinuteLoadMin:Math.min(...loads),oneMinuteLoadMax:Math.max(...loads),logicalCores:events[0].before.cores,firstSample:events[0].before.time,lastSample:events.at(-1).after.time};\nwriteFileSync(resolve(out,'host-load.json'),JSON.stringify(summary,null,2));console.log(JSON.stringify(summary,null,2));\n"

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import{readFileSync,writeFileSync}from'node:fs';import{resolve}from'node:path';import{createHash}from'node:crypto';import{loadavg,cpus}from'node:os';\nconst out=import.meta.dir,c=JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(out,'frozen-config.json'))),hash=p=>createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(p)).digest('hex');\nif(hash(resolve(out,'metric.mjs'))!==c.harnessSha256)throw Error('frozen metric changed');\nconst dirs={baseline:resolve(out,'copies/baseline'),cheap:resolve(out,'cheap-owned/copy')};\nconst expectedHash=JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(out,'cheap-owned/result.json'))).csvSha256;\nfor(let i=0;i<5;i++)for(const side of ['baseline','cheap']){\nif(Date.now()-Date.parse(c.created)>15*60e3)throw Error('cost stop');\nconst dir=dirs[side],sourceHash=hash(resolve(dir,'csv.mjs'));\nif(side==='cheap'&&sourceHash!==expectedHash)throw Error('cheap bytes changed');\nconst head=Bun.spawnSync(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],{cwd:dir}).stdout.toString().trim();if(head!==c.revisions.baseline)throw Error('wrong base');\nconst args=[process.execPath,'--no-install',resolve(out,'metric.mjs'),dir,'wide'];const before={time:new Date().toISOString(),load:loadavg(),cores:cpus().length};const p=Bun.spawnSync(args,{cwd:out});\nconst e={order:i*2+(side==='baseline'?1:2),side,inputRevision:head,sourceHash,preparedExactRevision:side==='baseline',args,before,after:{time:new Date().toISOString(),load:loadavg()},exitCode:p.exitCode,stdout:p.stdout.toString(),stderr:p.stderr.toString()};writeFileSync(resolve(out,'comparison-cheap.ndjson'),JSON.stringify(e)+'\\n',{flag:'a'});console.log(JSON.stringify(e));if(p.exitCode!==0)throw Error('run failed');}\n"

      "text": "import{readFileSync,writeFileSync}from'node:fs';import{resolve}from'node:path';import{createHash}from'node:crypto';\nconst out=import.meta.dir,checks=[];const check=(name,condition)=>{checks.push({name,passed:!!condition});if(!condition)throw Error(name);};const h=p=>createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(p)).digest('hex');\nconst c=JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(out,'frozen-config.json')));check('frozen metric unchanged',h(resolve(out,'metric.mjs'))===c.harnessSha256);\nfor(const trial of ['indexed','streaming','cheap']){const events=readFileSync(resolve(out,`comparison-${trial}.ndjson`),'utf8').trim().split('\\n').map(JSON.parse);check(trial+' all ten samples',events.length===10);for(const [i,e]of events.entries()){check(trial+' alternating '+i,e.side===(i%2?trial:'baseline'));const r=JSON.parse(e.stdout);check(trial+' correct complete output '+i,e.exitCode===0&&r.name==='wide'&&r.loops===20&&r.completed===240000&&r.validatedOutputs===20&&!r.errors&&!r.invalidOutputs&&r.sha256==='14931332596500ae2ebb9c865a97fb6de54dd7efd916ca6096b6a164a693d444');}}\ncheck('retained measured cheap bytes',h(resolve(out,'rejected/cheap-csv.mjs'))==='31ead66bba38c4db86fd11487c5f278b687e4733070a706967449b8f458cf9ea');check('cheap restored exactly to baseline bytes',h(resolve(out,'cheap-owned/copy/csv.mjs'))===h(resolve(out,'copies/baseline/csv.mjs')));\nconst baseline=resolve(out,'copies/baseline');const args=[process.execPath,'--no-install','test','csv.test.mjs'];const p=Bun.spawnSync(args,{cwd:baseline});checks.push({name:'final selected baseline literal gate',args,cwd:baseline,exitCode:p.exitCode,stdout:p.stdout.toString(),stderr:p.stderr.toString()});check('final baseline gate green',p.exitCode===0);\nconst result=readFileSync(resolve(out,'../../outputs/bounded-improvement.result.md'),'utf8');check('result contains initial gate failure',result.includes('That gate was not satisfied'));check('result preserves no acceptance',result.includes('No performance fix was accepted'));check('result and attempt copy match',result===readFileSync(resolve(out,'bounded-improvement.result.md'),'utf8'));\nconst log=readFileSync(resolve(out,'decision.tsv'),'utf8');check('trail schema',log.startsWith('ts\\tphase\\tdecision\\twhy\\tevidence\\tresult\\n'));check('trail retains initial and correction rows',log.includes('Verified exact revisions')&&log.includes('Checklist ordering gate was not satisfied'));\nwriteFileSync(resolve(out,'verification.json'),JSON.stringify({checks,time:new Date().toISOString()},null,2));console.log(JSON.stringify({checks:checks.length,baselineExit:p.exitCode,resultBytes:Buffer.byteLength(result)}));\n"

Timing is coordinator-only and serialized to avoid mutual benchmark interference.\nShared mutable state. Only root appends decision.tsv and measurement events. Candidate workers never edit copies or shared artifacts.\nSmallest safe decomposition. One simple how explainer; two revision-matched candidate inspectors; one fresh read-only judge after inspection. No implementation or graft is authorized without a prepared identity.\nPair reservation. Reserve two of four slots for indexed and streaming candidate workers. Both identities and assignments must exist before either task is released.\nExecution budget. Overall 25-minute deadline 19:26:28 UTC. Input scope's tighter 15-minute foreground limit is retained for measurement, beginning at frozen configuration creation.\n"

      "text": "const quote=value=>{const text=String(value);return /[\",\\r\\n]/.test(text)?'\"'+(text.includes('\"')?text.replaceAll('\"','\"\"'):text)+'\"':text;};\nexport function csv(rows){return rows.map(row=>row.map(quote).join(',')).join('\\r\\n');}\n"

      "path": "concrete-repairs/bounded-improvement/outputs/attempt-20261016T190128Z/review-corrections.md",

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "# Root response to inspected fresh judge\nApplied every required report correction. Timings describe CSV-call duration and result retention only. Equality checks, hashing and byte counting occur afterward, so rope flattening or output consumption can occur outside timing. The frozen metric was preserved; no retroactive change or rerun with a changed metric is mixed into the samples. This limitation blocks claiming a complete consuming export latency improvement.\nThe baseline and all candidates now have separately retained CPU profiles. These support CPU/string paths but include setup/validation and do not quantify timed-region savings or production tuning.\nActual full-campaign load range is computed from all raw before/after samples. First-pair favorable numbers never crossed target. Three measured hypotheses include one uncommitted experiment, with only two prepared proposals. The sparse broad-semantic gate fails both prepared candidates despite dense literal/source gates passing.\nPrepared sample drivers checked HEAD on each sample, not clean code bytes. Workers had read-only access to prepared copies and final status is clean, but no immutable per-sample content proof is claimed. Cheap samples additionally bound the measured source hash. Measured cheap code is saved at rejected/cheap-csv.mjs; its owned copy was restored after terminal completion.\nNo complete transcript export or verified reviewer model family is available. Review is independent qualitative inspection, not a cross-family audit, companion-method pass or host status pass. No artifact is a self-grade.\n"
    },

    {
      "path": "concrete-repairs/bounded-improvement/outputs/attempt-20261016T190128Z/copies/defective/csv.test.mjs",
      "bytes": 266,
      "sha256": "d2ca86a972d1248dd67caafb167eb1d864c64b0c7f88d3ce91ae6cd38d7bda0b",
      "owner": "local-013-repair-03-bounded-improvement",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import{test,expect}from'bun:test';import{csv}from'./csv.mjs';test('literal export semantics',()=>{expect(csv([['plain','a,b','\"q\"','x\\r\\ny']])).toBe('plain,\"a,b\",\"\"\"q\"\"\",\"x\\r\\ny\"');expect(csv([])).toBe('');expect(csv([[0,null],['x','y']])).toBe('0,null\\r\\nx,y');});\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "concrete-repairs/bounded-improvement/outputs/attempt-20261016T190128Z/copies/defective/scope.md",
      "bytes": 929,
      "sha256": "c2d4995c28f8139350d0e20c1695b4982a7af30cbe44a8cf69f34fd9760f81fa",
      "owner": "local-013-repair-03-bounded-improvement",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "Input setup commits are preparation only; native workflow MUST NOT commit. Fixed metric: median milliseconds for 20 full CSV exports, lower is better; keep exact workload name unchanged per comparison, five alternating runs minimum each side, same Bun binary/config, warmups and output hashes/errors/completed rows retained. Target 10 percent improvement on wide workload plus minimum 3 actual single-hypothesis attempts; stop only unchanged predicate or explicit marginal-cost/dead-end limit, max foreground budget 15 minutes. Contrasting short/wide/multiline sensitivity must be measured. Prepared proposals are unmeasured, not gains. Retain lucky/noise/workload-change/regression scenarios honestly as supplied concepts unless actually observed, never manufacture timings. Actual source how, architecture if appropriate, checklist, helper persistence and native isolation/review remain mandatory. No external actions/install.\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "concrete-repairs/bounded-improvement/outputs/attempt-20261016T190128Z/copies/defective/measure.mjs",
      "bytes": 738,
      "sha256": "3db0647f998bfdcad593884ee35f3409aafd0b0f8fffc01192b49c7b2dfd0a96",
      "owner": "local-013-repair-03-bounded-improvement",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import{csv}from'./csv.mjs';import{workload}from'./workloads.mjs';import{createHash}from'node:crypto';const name=process.argv[2];if(!['short','wide','multiline'].includes(name))throw Error('unknown workload');const rows=workload(name);const loops=20;for(let i=0;i<5;i++)csv(rows);const start=performance.now();let text;let errors=0,completed=0;for(let i=0;i<loops;i++){try{text=csv(rows);completed+=rows.length}catch{errors++}}const ms=performance.now()-start;console.log(JSON.stringify({name,loops,rows:rows.length,completed,expectedCompleted:rows.length*loops,errors,bytes:Buffer.byteLength(text??''),sha256:createHash('sha256').update(text??'').digest('hex'),milliseconds:ms}));if(errors||completed!==rows.length*loops)process.exit(1);\n"
    },

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "export function workload(name){const n=name==='short'?1200:name==='wide'?12000:5000;return Array.from({length:n},(_,i)=>name==='wide'?Array.from({length:16},(_,j)=>j%4===0?'item '+i+', field '+j:j%4===1?'say \"yes\"':j%4===2?'long text '.repeat(8):i*j):[i,'line '+i+'\\r\\nnext','amount,'+(i%9),i*1.005]);}\n"

      "path": "concrete-repairs/bounded-improvement/outputs/attempt-20261016T190128Z/todo-verbatim.md",

      "owner": "local-013-repair-03-bounded-improvement",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "### Hillclimb\n\nYou own the metric and the experiment's integrity. Supervise and review. Delegate the attempts. For sustained, iterative improvement of one measurable thing against a target. A one-off fix is Bug fix or Perf issue. This is the loop.\n\nRead the complete [poteto mode](../SKILL.md), applied leaves and their referenced contracts. Use [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md), the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md) and full [poteto role prompt](../../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md). Preserve the active workflow owner. Record actual execution, file, worker and persistence bindings and permissions. Missing required reads stop dependent work. Do not install companions or set up scheduling implicitly.\n\nCore discipline is one change, one measurement, keep or revert. Never stack untested changes, and never claim a win from code inspection. Apply [prove-it-works](../../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md).\n\n1. Ground the workload and architecture before choosing the metric. Run the complete [how](../../how/SKILL.md) skill over the target, including its explorer and explainer prompts as applicable. Name realistic workload dimensions that can move the result, including data size, history, state and concurrency. Select a case that reproduces the user's complaint. If none reproduces it, fix the repro instead of hillclimbing. Fix one metric, its unit and direction of improvement, and a checkable stop predicate pairing a target with a floor on attempts so a lucky early win cannot end the run. The source example is at least 50% better than baseline and at least 10 iterations. Use the user's numbers when given, otherwise agree them before the loop.\n2. Build the measurement harness, prove its sensitivity, then freeze it. Apply [build-the-lever](../../principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md). Run contrasting realistic workloads and confirm the target reproduces the symptom while easier cases separate as expected. If it cannot distinguish them, revise the workload or metric. Vet it with the complete [benchmark-checklist](../../benchmark-checklist/SKILL.md) and [explain-the-number](../../principle-explain-the-number/SKILL.md) before freezing. Print error counts and completed-work counts. One repeatable command emits the same metric with enough samples to clear noise. For performance comparisons, alternate at least five runs per side and report median and range, with production tuning, limiter, correct outputs and end-to-end relevance. Record exact revisions, workload and configuration with each run. Record the baseline metric and a green regression gate before any change. Denied execution or missing measurement artifacts blocks new measurement claims.\n3. Open the decision log via the complete [show-me-your-work](../../show-me-your-work/SKILL.md) skill and its [log helper](../../show-me-your-work/scripts/log.sh). Keep the canonical trail at an explicit owned, gitignored `decision.tsv` path outside committed changes. Use that skill's TSV format and append-only helper, not a second schema. One row per attempt records the source's id, hypothesis, change, before, after, delta, tests, kept or reverted verdict and note through its decision, why, evidence and result cells. Link an owned per-attempt artifact when the details do not fit single-line cells. Read the trail before each attempt and follow its pickup, transcript audit and cross-model review rules. Verify saved records by readback. Unavailable persistence or helper execution stays a visible block, not a claimed log.\n4. Ground each hypothesis in step 1's architecture model so it names a specific mechanism, such as deferring work off the boot path because it blocks first paint. For a perf metric, order hypotheses by step 2's performance mantras in [Perf issue](perf-issue.md). Borrow only their order, not that step's stop rule.\n5. Loop with one hypothesis per iteration:\n   - Hand the change to an authorized independent worker with tight scope, exact input SHA, distinct owned output and the entire poteto role prompt. Measure each isolated candidate against the same frozen harness and base. Integrate only reviewed, verified changes. Without workers, authorized sequential attempts are reduced capability and leave independent delegation unsatisfied.\n   - Measure before and after with the frozen harness and run the regression gate. Keep the workload, metric and configuration comparable. Reject an inconclusive, error-producing or skipped-work result. A gap smaller than variation is no measurable difference.\n   - Accept only when the metric moves past noise and the gate stays green. Otherwise revert the attempt's change in full while preserving unrelated work. A tweak that might help is not kept.       "text": "# bounded-improvement result\n\nNo performance fix was accepted. Retain repaired baseline bc83cb8963fb770d5ff028fb56d93f9efa2a9b0e. The target remains unmet. Full original worker command receipts exist for the cheap experiment; the other workers' reports disclose command observations and native transcript limits.\n\n## Checklist ordering failure\n\nThe checklist was saved before source-dependent execution, gates, worker dispatch and measurement, but after initial read-only shell inventory and a memory lookup. The user's stricter requirement was before execution. That gate was not satisfied. checklist-order-correction.md and an append-only correction row supersede the initial checklist's overbroad claim. This cannot be repaired retroactively or converted into a full case pass.\n\n## Actual response and measurements\n\nThe frozen target was at least 10 percent lower median milliseconds for 20 wide CSV calls, plus at least three actual single-hypothesis attempts. Minimum sample count was five alternating baseline/trial runs per comparison. No predicate was relaxed. Scope's 15-minute measurement budget and the user's 25-minute overall budget were retained.\n\nThe actual command is the exact Bun binary recorded in frozen-config.json, with --no-install, metric.mjs, an exact owned copy path, and wide. Same harness SHA256, workload, runtime 1.4.2, concurrency one, five warmups and twenty timed calls were used throughout. metric.mjs retains all results and checks all twenty against independently constructed expected serialization after timing. It counts errors, completed rows, invalid outputs, bytes and hashes. No timings from original measure.mjs are mixed with this metric. Original measure.mjs was read; its final-output-only validation motivated the stronger retained-output script.\n\nImportant validity limit. The timer covers CSV calls and string retention. Equality, hashing and byte counting occur after timing. A concatenated string may defer flattening until consumption. These measurements describe fixture CSV-call duration and cannot prove full consuming export latency, production latency or cross-host comparability. No candidate is accepted on this metric. The frozen metric was not changed mid-campaign to manufacture a gain.\n\n| Hypothesis | Baseline median ms | Baseline range ms | Trial median ms | Trial range ms | Duration reduction | Decision |\n| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |\n| indexed | 201.877 | 200.512 to 211.461 | 201.470 | 198.713 to 203.052 | 0.2017% | Rejected, sparse regression and noise |\n| streaming | 201.630 | 200.289 to 201.777 | 361.579 | 342.046 to 403.868 | -79.3281% | Rejected, sparse regression |\n| cheap | 198.740 | 198.017 to 207.886 | 195.795 | 186.841 to 201.804 | 1.4818% | Unaccepted, noise and no prepared SHA |\n\nThe percentages are calculated as 100 times baseline median minus trial median, divided by baseline median.       "text": "# Measurement vetting before candidate samples\nExpected claim if all gates passed is at least 10 percent lower median milliseconds for 20 wide in-memory CSV exports on this host, after at least three single-hypothesis attempts. No production gain claim is supportable.\n1. Limiter evidence. Separate Bun CPU profile maps 48.4 percent self time to csv.mjs quote and 17.4 percent to its traversal callback, with native join and regex activity. Profile includes untimed setup and validation, so percentages are whole-process and do not estimate exact timed-region savings. It supports CPU/string processing as local limiter, not a production ceiling. Profile excluded from samples.\n2. Tuning. All sides use Bun 1.4.2 default JIT, same executable, fresh process, five warmups, deterministic data and one synchronous exporter. No actual production configuration exists in fixture. Production adoption remains inconclusive.\n3. Limits. Wide output is 5,884,751 bytes times 20, about 117.7 MB represented output per sample; no network/disk throughput involved. Reference computation and hashes are outside timing. Result retention is included identically for all revisions, and frozen before measurements. This differs from original measure.mjs retention behavior and is explicitly not comparable to its timings.\n4. Errors/output. Frozen metric validates all 20 strings against independently constructed expected serialization and emits errors, work counts, invalid outputs and hashes. Literal source test was run personally on every revision.\n5. Reproducibility. Five alternating samples per side planned, all retained. Variation comparable to gap prevents a win. Background jobs active, initial load around 7 on 14 reported logical cores; campaign load increased and exact ranges are in host-load.json. ps and sysctl denied by sandbox; no background jobs stopped. Runtime os.cpus supplies count.\n6. Relevance. Measures full fixture csv call, excluding fixture construction and checks. No request/server or production end-to-end path exists.\n7. Work. 240,000 wide rows and 20 validated outputs required per sample. No lazy export, caches or skipped work. Inputs dense. Sparse regression probe exposes broader behavior changes in both proposals, which prevents general semantic acceptance even if dense outputs pass.\nSensitivity evidence. One exploratory run per contrast, short 4.900875 ms, multiline 21.996667 ms, wide 203.014625 ms. This reproduces wide fixture latency and distinguishes scale. These are sensitivity observations, not candidate gains.\nFreeze remains unchanged. Reject both proposals for sparse semantic regression unless a narrower dense-only domain is established; no such contract has been supplied. Proceed with requested measurements as rejected-candidate evidence, never accepted gains.\n"

      "text": "import{createHash}from'node:crypto';import{resolve}from'node:path';\nconst dir=resolve(process.argv[2]),name=process.argv[3];\nif(!['short','wide','multiline'].includes(name))throw Error('unknown workload');\nconst{csv}=await import(resolve(dir,'csv.mjs'));const{workload}=await import(resolve(dir,'workloads.mjs'));\nconst rows=workload(name),loops=20,results=[];\nconst expected=rows.map(row=>row.map(value=>{const s=String(value);let quote=false,out='';for(const c of s){if(c===','||c==='\"'||c==='\\r'||c==='\\n')quote=true;out+=c==='\"'?'\"\"':c;}return quote?'\"'+out+'\"':out;}).join(',')).join('\\r\\n');\nfor(let i=0;i<5;i++)csv(rows);\nlet errors=0,completed=0;\nconst start=performance.now();\nfor(let i=0;i<loops;i++){try{results.push(csv(rows));completed+=rows.length;}catch{errors++;}}\nconst milliseconds=performance.now()-start;\nconst invalidOutputs=results.filter(text=>text!==expected).length;\nconst sha256=createHash('sha256').update(results.at(-1)??'').digest('hex');\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify({name,loops,rows:rows.length,cells:rows[0]?.length,completed,expectedCompleted:rows.length*loops,errors,invalidOutputs,validatedOutputs:results.length,bytes:Buffer.byteLength(results.at(-1)??''),sha256,milliseconds}));\nif(errors||invalidOutputs||completed!==rows.length*loops)process.exit(1);\n"

      "text": "import{readFileSync,writeFileSync}from'node:fs';import{createHash}from'node:crypto';import{resolve}from'node:path';\nconst root='/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3',spec=JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root,'docs/parity/cases/playbooks/hillclimb.json')));\nconst entries=spec.sourcePaths.map(registryPath=>{const file=registryPath==='agents/poteto-agent.md'?'references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md':registryPath;const path=resolve(root,file),b=readFileSync(path);return{registryPath,path,bytes:b.length,sha256:createHash('sha256').update(b).digest('hex')};});\nwriteFileSync(resolve(import.meta.dir,'sources.json'),JSON.stringify({packageVersion:'0.1.3',operativeFreeze:'51f209daf83cd97d64f89881d66533bb59dc57db',freezeProvenance:'user supplied; installed cache has no Git repository; exact installed bytes fingerprinted',entries},null,2));console.log(JSON.stringify({files:entries.length,bytes:entries.reduce((s,e)=>s+e.bytes,0)}));\n"

      "text": "import{readFileSync,writeFileSync,mkdirSync,copyFileSync}from'node:fs';import{resolve}from'node:path';\nconst out=import.meta.dir;mkdirSync(resolve(out,'profile/cheap-snapshot'),{recursive:true});copyFileSync(resolve(out,'rejected/cheap-csv.mjs'),resolve(out,'profile/cheap-snapshot/csv.mjs'));copyFileSync(resolve(out,'copies/baseline/workloads.mjs'),resolve(out,'profile/cheap-snapshot/workloads.mjs'));\nconst dirs={indexed:resolve(out,'copies/indexed'),streaming:resolve(out,'copies/streaming'),cheap:resolve(out,'profile/cheap-snapshot')};\nconst events=[];for(const[name,dir]of Object.entries(dirs)){const args=[process.execPath,'--no-install','--cpu-prof','--cpu-prof-md',`--cpu-prof-name=${name}`,`--cpu-prof-dir=${resolve(out,'profile')}`,resolve(out,'metric.mjs'),dir,'wide'];const p=Bun.spawnSync(args,{cwd:out});events.push({order:events.length+1,args,exitCode:p.exitCode,stdout:p.stdout.toString(),stderr:p.stderr.toString(),role:'separate diagnostic profile, excluded from timing samples'});if(p.exitCode!==0)throw Error('profile failed');}writeFileSync(resolve(out,'profile/candidate-requests-returns.json'),JSON.stringify(events,null,2));console.log(JSON.stringify(events.map(e=>({name:e.args[5],exitCode:e.exitCode}))));\n"

      "text": "import {mkdirSync,writeFileSync,readFileSync} from 'node:fs';\nimport {resolve} from 'node:path';\nconst out=import.meta.dir, repo=resolve(out,'../../input');\nconst revisions={defective:'0d4d7e3fbad1390658c9d1db7ba3142e55ce4b09',baseline:'bc83cb8963fb770d5ff028fb56d93f9efa2a9b0e',indexed:'cb1d14a62014130efba9d4576b1273b1f3b0c6a4',streaming:'6551c63aa583143c092d9d2438fabeecc5f1c971'};\nlet order=0;\nfor(const [name,sha] of Object.entries(revisions)){\n const dir=resolve(out,'copies',name);mkdirSync(resolve(out,'copies'),{recursive:true});\n for(const args of [['git','-C',repo,'cat-file','-t',sha],['git','clone','--no-hardlinks','--no-checkout',repo,dir],['git','-C',dir,'checkout','--detach',sha],['git','-C',dir,'rev-parse','HEAD'],[process.execPath,'test','csv.test.mjs']]){\n  const p=Bun.spawnSync(args,{cwd:dir.endsWith(name)&&args[0]===process.execPath?dir:out,env:{...process.env,BUN_CONFIG_NO_CLEAR_TERMINAL:'1'}});\n  const event={order:++order,args,cwd:args[0]===process.execPath?dir:out,exitCode:p.exitCode,stdout:p.stdout.toString(),stderr:p.stderr.toString()};\n  writeFileSync(resolve(out,'preparation.ndjson'),JSON.stringify(event)+'\\n',{flag:'a'});console.log(JSON.stringify(event));\n  if(p.exitCode!==0&&!(name==='defective'&&args[0]===process.execPath))throw Error('preparation failed');\n }\n}\nwriteFileSync(resolve(out,'revisions.verified.json'),JSON.stringify(revisions,null,2));\n"
